characters.description: A tower climber held in a stone cell by a silver-eyed captor of overwhelming power. Max masks the extent of his abilities, stays calm under pressure, and waits for an opening while worrying about Tanila and the companions from whom he has been separated.
characters.name: Max

characters.description: The sentient ability bound within Max. It speaks to him internally, assesses magical dangers, and counsels patience while he is imprisoned. The entity shares his concern for Tanila and the companions from whom Max has been separated.
characters.name: Consume

characters.description: The immensely powerful man holding Max behind a magical barrier. He tries to frighten and provoke his prisoner, but Max suspects that fear lies beneath his anger. His strength makes a direct escape attempt too dangerous.
characters.name: Silver-eyed captor

characters.description: A lizard woman freed by Max from slavers in a mountain cave. She accepts the name Amy and agrees to guide him toward a city where someone may be able to remove his collar, giving him vital local knowledge during the hunt.
characters.name: Amy

characters.description: Amy's blind mother, who is wary when her daughter arrives at their glass settlement with Max, an unfamiliar smooth-skinned outsider.
characters.name: Amy's mother

characters.description: The powerful insect who runs the third-ring arena and negotiates a contract giving Max a share of his winnings, with improved terms for victories and a champion defeat.
characters.name: Third-ring arena proprietor

characters.description: The arena identity Max adopts when he begins fighting for tokens. He presents Ifrit as a fire-wielding combatant while concealing his wider range of powers and his real reason for trying to advance through the city.
characters.name: Ifrit

characters.description: A local craftsperson whom Max approaches for a strong but unadorned staff. The weaponsmith is willing to consider the unusual commission, opening a possible route to equipment suited to Max's needs.
characters.name: Kimono-mimi weaponsmith

characters.description: Max's bonded partner and a member of his tower party. Two months after his disappearance, she leads the group's continued climb and trusts the unchanged sign of their bond as evidence that he is still alive.
characters.name: Tanila

characters.description: A returning member of Max's tower party who continues climbing while Max is missing. After the group clears the floor-45 boss, Fowl supports Tanila's conviction that their absent companion remains alive.
characters.name: Fowl

characters.description: A returning member of Max's tower party who helps defeat the floor-45 boss during his absence. Batrire stands with Tanila and the others as they continue the climb without abandoning hope of finding him.
characters.name: Batrire

characters.description: One of the tower climbers traveling with Tanila's group during Max's unexplained absence. Cordelia takes part in their successful floor-45 battle as the party presses onward without him.
characters.name: Cordelia

characters.description: An ally fighting alongside Tanila, Fowl, Batrire, and Cordelia while Max is missing. Dexic helps the group defeat the floor-45 boss and remains with them as they continue their tower ascent.
characters.name: Dexic

characters.description: A promoter who provides lodging when Max and Amy reach a wealthier ring of the city. He also agrees to search for suitable premises for the weaponsmith.
characters.name: City promoter

characters.description: The golden-scaled ruler who controls the city and its arena system. She intervenes when arena protections are violated, recognizes that Max was brought to her world by the hunter, and postpones a private discussion with him.
characters.name: Dragonkin ruler

characters.description: A formidable Vorpal hunter who becomes Ifrit's representative under a profit-sharing agreement. Despite his rabbit-like appearance, he makes clear that he can defend the new arrangement and supplies practical support as Max advances.
characters.name: Jazz Jack

characters.description: The private name Max gives Consume, the sentient ability within him. Their bond has developed through danger and Max's choices, and the name marks a more personal understanding between them that Max does not extend to anyone else.
characters.name: Bob

characters.description: A red-skinned extraplanar fighter called through Max's demonic summoning. It recognizes Max and says his blood altered it, then accepts a tightly limited bargain to kill seven arena opponents before the contract expires.
characters.name: Summoned demon

characters.description: A lionkin arena champion matched against Ifrit. Shamina enters heavily armed with sword, shield, and armor, presenting a physically imposing challenge as Max reaches a more dangerous level of competition.
characters.name: Shamina

characters.description: A servant of the city ruler who takes Max alone to her portal-filled residence. The attendant rejects being reduced to a simple elf label.
characters.name: Dark elf attendant

characters.description: An experienced craftswoman from another world who recognizes the unusual nature of Max's bonded staff. She privately agrees to exchange materials and instruction for access to his uncommon crafting knowledge.
characters.name: Dwarven weaponsmith

characters.description: The unidentified traveler whom the dragonkin ruler says paid her to remove Max. This disclosure reveals that his imprisonment in the local tower is part of a deliberate arrangement extending beyond the ruler herself.
characters.name: Other world traveler

characters.description: A collared dragon imprisoned beyond the tower horde. He tells Max that the dragonkin ruler compels him to guard the exit and kill anyone who survives long enough to reach him.
characters.name: Silver dragon

characters.description: A Golden Axe leader connected to Max's climbing group. He is part of the established support structure surrounding the tower campaign before Max's disappearance in this volume.
characters.name: Everett

characters.description: A Golden Axe trainer and operational leader associated with Max and his fellow tower climbers. His role in their established organization predates the events of this volume.
characters.name: Tom

recaps.ending: Max kills the dragonkin ruler in a public arena battle and uses her powers to prevent the traveler behind his removal from escaping. Bob attacks the traveler and acquires the travel ability Max needs. Max declares himself the city's champion, appointing Jazz Jack to oversee civic affairs and the dark elf attendant to run the arena. He defeats Amy over her role in the first weaponsmith's murder and leaves her with Jazz Jack for execution. The city remains under Max's remote authority, while his promise of a future skill shard to Jazz Jack and his obligation to help the dwarven weaponsmith create two more weapons remain open. Max returns to his own world, races through tower floors 40 to 47, and reunites with Tanila, Fowl, Batrire, Cordelia, and Dexic on floor 48. They conceal his cross-world captivity behind a story of overseas travel. Tanila confirms that she carries Max's child, and they expect threats connected to both of them. The party will tackle floors 49 and 50 together. Bob withdraws to evolve, the silver dragon's living egg remains in Max's care, and the original silver-eyed hunter is still at large.
recaps.in_short: A silver-eyed hunter abducts Max and releases him into a hostile world under a binding collar. Max survives the wilderness, frees Amy, and enters a city where arena victories offer power and a possible route home. Fighting as Ifrit, he advances through increasingly lethal contests while learning local crafting and strengthening Consume, which he names Bob. Amy gains power but arranges their first weaponsmith's murder. The dragonkin ruler then traps Max in a tower on another traveler's orders. Max survives the horde, kills a coerced silver dragon after promising to save its egg, breaks his collar, and defeats the ruler in dragon form. He takes the traveler's world-crossing ability, places Jazz Jack and the dark elf attendant over the city, and leaves Amy for execution. Back home, Max rejoins Tanila's party on floor 48. Tanila is pregnant, Bob is evolving, and the reunited group plans to clear floors 49 and 50 together.

recaps.text: Previously: Max, also known as Seth Pendell, climbed the tower with Tanila, Fowl, Batrire, and Cordelia as part of the Golden Axe community. Tanila is his bonded partner, and their companions regard the group as a family. Dexic is an allied fighter with an earlier debt linking her to Max's party. Everett is a Golden Axe leader, while Tom trains climbers and helps direct operations. Max carries a sentient internal ability called Consume, which can advise him and turn defeated enemies into avenues for growth. The tower climb, Max's bonds with his companions, and the dangerous attention drawn by his unusual power all remain central as this volume begins.

A silver-eyed captor holds Max behind a magical barrier, tests his abilities, and reveals that someone paid to have him targeted. Rather than kill him immediately, the captor fits him with a collar that seals his storage and releases him into another world with a seven-day head start. Max survives the jungle and desert by improvising weapons, using magic, regenerating severe wounds, and drawing strength from defeated creatures. The collar suppresses his contact with Consume and leaves direct confrontation with the hunter impossible. Max interrupts a group of slavers and frees a lizard woman whom he calls Amy. She guides him across the desert toward a city where the collar might be removed. After a brief return, Consume warns that unseen powers are watching Max. Amy brings him to her glass settlement, where her mother explains the local order: power can be acquired and traded, a female ruler controls the tower and gladiatorial games, and tournament tokens may buy both collar removal and a source of power for Amy. With the hunter's deadline closing, Max accepts the city arenas as his best route forward.

Max protects Amy and her mother from a hostile sand wielder, then travels with Amy into the layered city. Because his collar marks him as a valuable captive, they hide it and use Amy's local knowledge to pass the gates. Max remains loyal to Tanila despite Amy's growing attachment. He adopts the arena name Ifrit and arranges a contract that will earn the tokens needed to advance. A kimono-mimi weaponsmith teaches him that local crafting consumes life force. Max combines that method with regeneration and elemental magic to create a bonded staff of exceptional quality. Elsewhere, two months have passed since his disappearance. Tanila, Fowl, Batrire, Cordelia, and Dexic defeat the floor-45 boss and continue believing he survives. Consume returns just before Max's first match. Max wins that fight and kills a much stronger stone master in his second, exposing more durability and magic than intended. His victories earn passage to the next city ring, but also spread word of the unusual smooth-skinned fighter. Max invites the weaponsmith to relocate with them as unknown observers begin following him and Amy.

In the wealthier rings, Max gains a promoter, improved equipment, and the attention of the golden-scaled ruler who controls the city. After relatives of a defeated fighter violate arena protections, the ruler intervenes and recognizes that the hunter brought Max into her world. Jazz Jack, a dangerous Vorpal hunter, becomes Max's representative and ties housing and support for the group to arena success. The promised workshop for Max's weaponsmith is secured, but the weaponsmith is murdered almost immediately. Max responds with a series of increasingly ruthless arena victories while seeking the killer and demanding protection for Amy. Consume warns that uncontrolled violent hunger could endanger Max's own friends. Amy is moved ahead and receives two power gems. Max privately gives Consume the name Bob. Deeper in the city, Jazz Jack explains that advancement is effectively permanent and that champions may come from other worlds. When Max is assigned seven opponents at once, he follows Bob's plan and summons a demon under a limited contract. The demon kills all seven, clashes briefly with the arriving ruler, and departs. The victory raises Max to another major strength threshold and leaves the inner arena wary of facing Ifrit.

Amy emerges from her enhancement with substantial power, takes a new identity, and leaves Max's group. Max then kills the lionkin champion Shamina after Bob pays a serious cost to reset his abilities. The win earns entry to the inner city, but the ruler demands three further victories before allowing tower access and leaves the eventual price of helping Max return home unstated. Jazz Jack accompanies Max into the sealed district, sacrificing an easy return to his own family. The ruler sends Max into a larger arena that draws fighters from many worlds. Max survives lethal matches against a flying combat machine and an armored insect, gaining broad language comprehension while continuing to hide his collar and regeneration. Bob's next evolution draws closer. Seeking a weapon able to penetrate stronger armor, Max forms a secret partnership with an experienced dwarven weaponsmith. They combine her rare materials with his elemental crafting methods to produce a bonded weapon that can shift among melee forms. In return, Max promises to help her make two additional weapons. He also reaches a major dexterity threshold, leaving him substantially faster and better equipped for the arena battles ahead.

Jazz Jack asks Max for a future skill shard so he can become strong enough to return to his wife and children, and Max agrees. After more victories, the ruler offers Max entry to the tower. Bob identifies the offer as a trap, but Max accepts. Inside, the ruler reveals that another world traveler paid her to remove him and that Amy arranged the first weaponsmith's murder. An apparently endless horde then keeps Max fighting for forty days. His summoned demon returns as a demon lord and clears a temporary path in exchange for later demon essence, with both sides accepting a mutual nonaggression pact. At the exit, Max finds a silver dragon enslaved by the ruler and forced to kill survivors because she holds his unhatched child. Max promises to rescue the egg. The dragon permits one free attack, and Max's Ultimate Form breaks his own collar before he kills the guardian. Free for the first time since his abduction, Max returns to the city, confirms Amy's responsibility, and coerces the ruler's attendant into helping him enter her estate. He recovers the living silver dragon egg and uses it as leverage to force the ruler into a public arena fight.

The dragonkin ruler enters the public match as an enormous golden dragon whose scales resist Max's first attacks. Her fire repeatedly inflicts fatal damage, but Bob spends stored power to refresh Max's defenses and abilities. Max eventually phases inside her body and destroys her heart. After killing the ruler, he acquires powers that can block system travel and uses them to trap the other world traveler who financed his removal. Bob attacks the traveler and takes the world-crossing ability Max needs. Max claims the city, appoints Jazz Jack to civic administration and the dark elf attendant to arena operations, and opens the local tower to capable challengers. He then defeats Amy over the weaponsmith's murder and leaves her to Jazz Jack for execution. Max returns home, clears floors 40 through 47 alone, and reaches his companions during their floor-48 battle. Bob withdraws to begin an evolution as Max reunites with Tanila, Fowl, Batrire, Cordelia, and Dexic. Back at Golden Axe, they agree to hide his imprisonment behind a claim of overseas travel. Tanila confirms her pregnancy. Expecting enemies to threaten their child, she and Max commit to becoming stronger, while the reunited party plans to clear floors 49 and 50 together.

characters.description: A young Accepted of the White Tower, close to being raised to full Aes Sedai. Of high Cairhienin noble blood and a niece of Cairhien's king, she is small, composed, quick-witted, and unusually strong in the One Power. Reserved and disciplined, she keeps her royal connections at arm's length and is devoted to her studies and to her closest friend, Siuan.
characters.name: Moiraine Damodred

characters.description: An Accepted of the White Tower and Moiraine's closest friend, a fisherman's daughter from the poor quarter of Tear with a blunt tongue, a quick mind, and one of the strongest gifts for the One Power seen in generations. Ambitious and shrewd, she is as fierce in argument as she is loyal in friendship, and as eager as Moiraine to earn the shawl of an Aes Sedai.
characters.name: Siuan Sanche

characters.description: The uncrowned king of Malkier, a northern realm swallowed by the Blight when he was an infant, raised by his people's survivors to a life of endless war against the Shadow. A peerless swordsman still young in years, grim, honorable, and expecting to die fighting in the Blight, he travels the Borderlands with an old shield-companion, bound by oaths older than himself.
characters.name: Lan Mandragoran

characters.description: The Amyrlin Seat, head of the Aes Sedai and ruler of the White Tower, a shrewd and formidable woman guiding the Tower through the upheaval of the Aiel War. Watchful and careful with her secrets, she wields the authority of her office with a firm and practiced hand.
characters.name: Tamra Ospenya

characters.description: An elderly Aes Sedai and trusted adviser to the Amyrlin, gifted with Foretelling, the rare and uncontrollable ability to speak true prophecy. Frail with age, she has spent her long life close to the seat of the Tower's power.
characters.name: Gitara Moroso

characters.description: The White Tower's Mistress of Novices, a calm, motherly Aes Sedai responsible for the discipline and welfare of novices and Accepted. Experienced and unruffled, she is a fixture of Tower life whose steady manner reassures the young women in her charge.
characters.name: Merean Redhill

characters.description: A famous and fearsome Aes Sedai of great reputation and long experience, blunt, imperious, and impossible to overawe. Already a legend among the sisters, she takes a sharp interest in the affairs of others and in the young women she encounters.
characters.name: Cadsuane Melaidhrin

characters.description: A grizzled Malkieri warrior and Lan's longtime shield-companion, one of the survivors who helped raise him after their homeland fell to the Blight. Loyal and hard-bitten, he keeps to the old customs and oaths of dead Malkier.
characters.name: Bukama Marenellin

recaps.ending: New Spring ends with the partnership that will drive the whole series into motion. Moiraine Damodred, now a full Aes Sedai, has survived an assassination attempt by a hidden servant of the Shadow and has committed herself to a lonely, secret quest: to find the infant boy prophesied to be the Dragon Reborn before the Shadow's agents can kill him, and one day to guide him toward the Last Battle. Lan Mandragoran, the last king of a nation devoured by the Blight, agrees to bond to her as her Warder, trading his expected death in the Blight for her cause. Her friend Siuan Sanche remains in the White Tower to hunt the Shadow's hidden agents from within and to rise in the Tower's ranks. As the book closes, Moiraine and Lan ride out together, beginning the long search that, years later, will bring them to a remote village and the young man born on that fateful day.
recaps.in_short: During the Aiel War, the Accepted Moiraine Damodred and Siuan Sanche are present when a dying Aes Sedai speaks a Foretelling: the Dragon has been Reborn, a boy child born that very day near the great battle. The Amyrlin swears the two friends to secrecy and quietly sets searchers to find the child, but soon the Amyrlin is dead and her searchers are being murdered, and Moiraine and Siuan realize that the Black Ajah, servants of the Shadow hidden among the Aes Sedai, are hunting anyone who knows. Newly raised to the shawl, Moiraine slips away from the Tower's dangerous politics to search for the child herself. In the Borderland city of Chachin she crosses paths with Lan Mandragoran, the uncrowned king of fallen Malkier and a deadly swordsman. Together they uncover and defeat a hidden servant of the Shadow sent to kill her. Recognizing they are stronger together, Moiraine asks Lan to become her Warder; he accepts, and the two set out in secret to find and protect the Dragon Reborn.

recaps.text: Set about twenty years before the main series, this book follows two young women of the White Tower, Moiraine Damodred and Siuan Sanche, as they near the end of their training to become Aes Sedai. The Aiel have come out of the Waste and are besieging the great island city of Tar Valon in the war that will be remembered as the Aiel War, and the Tower is crowded with the wounded and the anxious. Amid the chaos, the two friends, close as sisters despite Moiraine's noble birth and Siuan's humble one, are set to menial duties and chafe under the Tower's endless rules, unaware that the war's turning point is about to place them at the center of the most important secret of the age.

characters.description: An Army military police major selected for a concealed interagency assignment after completing a sensitive operation. He quickly recognizes that the supposed training course is a cover for work whose participants must remain unobtrusive.
characters.name: Jack Reacher

characters.description: An experienced FBI agent chosen for the same secret assignment as Jack Reacher and John White. Her recent success on a sensitive case and her deliberately inconspicuous position make her suitable for a tightly restricted investigation.
characters.name: Casey Waterman

characters.description: A CIA officer and analyst selected for the covert interagency unit alongside Jack Reacher and Casey Waterman. Like the others, he has been removed immediately after a successful sensitive assignment and placed under an ordinary-looking cover.
characters.name: John White

characters.description: The senior official who arrives under heavy security to direct the hidden assignment. He confirms that the stated training course is only operational cover and that the three selected investigators face a high-priority national-security problem.
characters.name: Alfred Ratcliffe

characters.description: Ratcliffe's senior deputy and the covert unit's operational authority. She briefs the investigators on an unidentified American offering an unknown item to a jihadist network for $100 million, while protecting a CIA source inside the Hamburg cell.
characters.name: Marian Sinclair

characters.description: A CIA-controlled source living inside a Hamburg sleeper cell with three Saudis. The source's safety is a central constraint on the investigation, preventing ordinary surveillance or intervention around the cell and its courier.
characters.name: Iranian double agent

characters.description: An unnamed Saudi courier who carries the unidentified American’s demand from Hamburg through the buyers’ network. His knowledge of the requested price makes him part of the tightly compartmented transaction.
characters.name: First Saudi courier

characters.description: Jack Reacher’s former top sergeant in the 110th military police unit and a trusted investigator. He encounters her at a diner in McLean.
characters.name: Neagley

characters.description: An unidentified American presented as the seller in the secret transaction. He intends to use the payment to buy an Argentine ranch and is linked to a murder in Hamburg.
characters.name: The American

characters.description: Casey Waterman's FBI support officer at the expanded joint control center. Landry helps run the domestic side of the data-intensive search while the field investigators pursue the unidentified American in Germany.
characters.name: Landry

characters.description: John White's CIA support officer in the joint control center. Vanderbilt works alongside Landry and Neagley as the inquiry begins narrowing a vast pool of Americans in Germany through travel and military records.
characters.name: Vanderbilt

characters.description: Hamburg's chief of detectives, overseeing the inquiry into a murdered woman. His investigation is compromised from the outset because he had a personal connection to the victim and redirects scrutiny to keep that relationship hidden.
characters.name: Griezman

characters.description: A U.S. Army air-defense soldier who has been absent without leave for four months. His possible access to a Chaparral system draws scrutiny, although that bulky and conspicuous equipment initially appears unable to explain the proposed sale.
characters.name: Wiley

characters.description: A Hamburg sewer-department clerical supervisor who witnessed an American meeting a Saudi contact in a bar. His detailed recollection provides the investigators with a physical description and a way to test their programmer theory.
characters.name: Helmut Klopp

characters.description: A courier sent from Jalalabad to tell the unidentified American that his buyers accept the offer.
characters.name: Female courier

characters.description: A former member of Jack Reacher's 110th unit who can provide discreet Army assistance in Hamburg. He takes custody of two military-connected gun traffickers and agrees to investigate their criminal bar without exposing the larger inquiry.
characters.name: Manuel Orozco

characters.description: The CIA station chief responsible for monitoring the Hamburg safe house. He reports an irregular change in the cell's window signal, a possible indication that the courier has arrived under altered circumstances.
characters.name: Bishop

characters.description: The AWOL air-defense private conclusively identified as the American seen meeting a Saudi contact in Hamburg. His personnel photograph matches the witness sketch, shifting the operation from an identity search to surveillance of his next contact.
characters.name: Horace Wiley

characters.description: A Hamburg shoe importer involved with the far-right group behind the bar. He considers taking over Wiley's transaction for his own organization and also wants retaliation against Jack Reacher and Neagley.
characters.name: Dremmler

characters.description: A Hamburg police officer secretly assisting Dremmler’s group. He helps investigate the American operation from inside law enforcement and gives Dremmler the investigators’ hotel location.
characters.name: Muller

characters.description: Horace Wiley’s former air-defense crewmate. He describes Wiley as secretive and intent on serving in Germany, and recalls his repeated references to Uncle Arnold, ranching, and Davy Crockett.
characters.name: Coleman

characters.description: A retired Army airborne infantry NCO who lived with Wiley's mother during part of Wiley's childhood. Investigators seek him in Germany because he may explain Wiley's repeated references to ranching and Davy Crockett.
characters.name: Arnold Peter Mason

characters.description: An active Army major general and former airborne officer identified as a possible source on Arnold Peter Mason's old unit. The investigators arrange a direct interview with him to determine what Mason's Davy Crockett stories meant.
characters.name: Wilson T. Helmsworth

characters.description: A false-document supplier connected to Helmut Klopp's bar. He is found murdered after his identification records are removed, and a fingerprint from his file storage connects him to evidence from the earlier Hamburg homicide.
characters.name: Wolfgang Schlupp

characters.description: Manuel Orozco's sergeant and driver, brought into the dockside warehouse entry. He joins Jack Reacher, Neagley, and Orozco as they infiltrate Dremmler's shoe-handling operation to search for the stolen van.
characters.name: Hooper

recaps.ending: Dremmler's group steals Wiley's van after the nuclear cargo has been loaded, and Wiley dies from a stabbing before the shipment can be recovered. Jack Reacher, Neagley, Manuel Orozco, and Hooper locate nine weapons in Dremmler's warehouse and the tenth device with its code file in his office. Once Reacher establishes that Dremmler's random switch movements did not arm it, he kills Dremmler and returns the complete set for emergency removal. The female courier surrenders, and her intelligence lets the CIA seize $600 million. The Saudi operatives are recalled to Yemen, while the Iranian double agent is extracted and relocated to the United States. Two months later, Reacher, Neagley, Orozco, and Hooper receive Army Commendation Medals, and Wilson T. Helmsworth receives a Silver Star. Reacher and Marian Sinclair begin a relationship. The wider buyer network, Dremmler's remaining organization, police corruption, and Wiley's Argentine property remain only partly resolved.
recaps.in_short: Jack Reacher joins FBI agent Casey Waterman and CIA officer John White in a secret unit investigating an American who has offered an unknown item to jihadist buyers for $100 million. Reacher and Neagley pursue the seller in Hamburg, identify him as AWOL soldier Horace Wiley, and discover that he stole ten portable Davy Crockett nuclear weapons hidden by an old inventory error. Wiley prepares an airborne transfer, but Dremmler's far-right organization hijacks the loaded van and fatally stabs him. Reacher, Neagley, Manuel Orozco, and Hooper find nine weapons in Dremmler's warehouse and the tenth with its arming file in his office. After confirming the device is safe, Reacher kills Dremmler, and the full set is removed. The courier's intelligence produces a $600 million CIA seizure, the Iranian source is resettled, and the recovery team is decorated, although parts of both hostile networks remain unresolved.

recaps.text: Previously: Jack Reacher is the continuing central figure in the series.

Jack Reacher receives a second Legion of Merit and is sent to what appears to be an interagency course. He quickly recognizes the cover. FBI agent Casey Waterman, CIA officer John White, and Reacher have each been taken from a recent success to form an unusually discreet unit under Alfred Ratcliffe and Marian Sinclair. Their problem is an unidentified American who met a Saudi courier near a Hamburg sleeper cell and demanded $100 million for an unknown item. A CIA-controlled Iranian inside the cell must be protected, sharply limiting surveillance. Reacher recruits his former sergeant Neagley, and they begin working through travel, military, banking, and equipment records. Their first visit to Hamburg fails to locate the meeting place. A theory involving compromised Y2K software then redirects the larger inquiry toward American programmers, despite Reacher's doubts. The urgency increases when the prospective buyers accept the seller's price.

The inquiry follows both the programmer theory and a Hamburg witness report. Chief detective Griezman is handling the murder of a woman connected to the unidentified American, although he has compromised that case to conceal his own relationship with the victim. A bar witness, Helmut Klopp, gives a detailed description of the American who met a Saudi contact. Jack Reacher and Neagley return with photographs of two hundred programmers, but Klopp rejects every one. Reacher concludes that the feared software plot and the $100 million offer are separate matters. The American seller remains unknown, while his risk of exposure grows through the homicide evidence and Klopp’s eyewitness description. The buyers kill the previous messenger to contain knowledge of the price and dispatch a female courier from Jalalabad to tell the American that his offer has been accepted.

Jack Reacher and Neagley use Klopp's account, a police sketch, and evidence from the murdered woman's car to pursue the seller. Two military-connected gun traffickers confirm that the same American has visited the bar and may have obtained German false documents there. Manuel Orozco quietly investigates that criminal link. Marian Sinclair joins the field team as the false-identity problem weakens their travel searches. A distinctive photograph of an AWOL air-defense crew leads Reacher toward Wiley, while a clandestine fingerprint check and Hamburg police surveillance create friction between Reacher and Sinclair. CIA station chief Bishop reports an irregular safe-house signal as the replacement courier arrives. The Army file finally identifies the sketched American as Horace Wiley, a thirty-five-year-old air-defense private absent without leave for four months. With the seller identified, the team prepares to follow his Saudi contact toward the next rendezvous, but still does not know what he is selling.

The investigators place the Hamburg safe house under German surveillance and examine Horace Wiley's unusual military career. FBI records show earlier arrests involving stolen goods, none successfully prosecuted. The clandestine fingerprint comparison privately identifies Wiley as the Hamburg murderer, but Jack Reacher withholds that result from Griezman because the national-security operation still depends on Wiley remaining free. Reacher and Marian Sinclair also begin a sexual relationship. Surveillance misses the female courier when she leaves the safe house. She meets Wiley at a Reeperbahn club, tells him the eastern buyers accept both his price and the agreed delivery date, and departs for the airport before the team can intercept her. The transaction has therefore moved beyond negotiation, while the investigators still lack the cargo, timetable, and destination.

A second threat develops inside Hamburg. Shoe importer Dremmler and police officer Muller, members of a far-right network, investigate the American operation and consider taking Horace Wiley's deal. Muller leaks police information, including the investigators' hotel and traffic plans. Jack Reacher and Neagley survive an ambush by the group. Meanwhile, sightings and Army interviews show that Wiley deliberately sought a German posting and has long planned to buy a ranch in Argentina. The team traces his references to an Uncle Arnold and to Davy Crockett but does not yet understand them. Wiley rents a large panel van and retrieves it from a dockside warehouse where he has hidden a stolen furniture truck and its unknown cargo for months. His movement records point toward a little-used military storage site as the probable source. As the investigators close on his false identities, Wiley kills the document supplier and removes the records. Dremmler's organization is also closing in, creating the risk that it will interfere before the Americans identify or secure the cargo.

The FBI identifies Uncle Arnold as Arnold Peter Mason, a retired airborne NCO who lived with Horace Wiley's mother during Wiley's childhood. Mason is now severely impaired and cannot reliably explain the old Davy Crockett stories, so Neagley finds another veteran of his unit, Major General Wilson T. Helmsworth. While Hamburg police are diverted by a staged garage fire, Wiley disguises his panel van and transfers ten fifty-pound containers plus a coded file from the stolen furniture truck. Helmsworth explains that Davy Crockett was the name used for a portable Cold War nuclear weapon. Records indicate that an undocumented eleventh crate may have contained ten such devices and their arming codes, never included in either delivery or recovery totals. The team now understands that Wiley may be selling ten nuclear weapons rather than conventional military property. Jack Reacher also derives a likely current identity from Wiley's Texas background, giving the investigators a new way to locate him before he can export the shipment.

The team identifies Wiley's current identity as Isaac Herbert Kempner and finds his Hamburg apartment, but Wiley sees the police presence and escapes. Evidence there confirms his Argentine plans and connection to the coded file. Reacher and Neagley narrow the search to the dockside warehouse district and block its sole vehicle bridge. Wiley receives the $100 million payment, while the female courier returns with two armed airport workers to collect the van for airborne distribution. Dremmler has already arranged a compromised bridge officer and sends associates with a duplicate van key. Reacher and Neagley find Wiley critically wounded beside the emptied furniture-truck crate. Before dying, he says two Germans took the loaded van. Reacher kills the armed airport workers when they draw their weapons, and the courier surrenders. She contradicts the bridge officer's claim that no van passed. Wiley found the lost nuclear crate by tracing a historical transcription error, but all ten weapons are now missing in Hamburg.

Evidence of a duplicate key, a false bridge report, and leaked police information points the team toward Dremmler. Griezman identifies him as the influential leader of an organized nationalist group and controller of a large dockside shoe business. Manuel Orozco's team extracts the Iranian double agent, while the captured courier is held for transfer. With both governments seeking a quiet recovery, Jack Reacher concludes that Dremmler probably hid the stolen van at his own wharf operation. Reacher, Neagley, Orozco, and Orozco's sergeant Hooper enter the shoe warehouse after dark. They find the disguised van concealed behind stacked inventory and prepare to drive it out. Reacher stops the recovery when he counts only nine weapon packs. Hooper independently confirms that one device and the codebook are missing. The van has been located, but the absent tenth weapon creates a separate and immediate danger inside the warehouse.

Jack Reacher, Neagley, Manuel Orozco, and Hooper enter the concealed office suite and find Dremmler with two associates, the tenth Davy Crockett weapon, and its opened code file. The associates are detained, but Dremmler has already moved the device's switches. Reacher studies the arming procedure and waits long enough to establish that Dremmler's random manipulation has not activated it. Dremmler admits that he leads the exclusionary nationalist movement. Once the device is known to be safe, Reacher kills him and returns the tenth weapon and code file to the van. A specialist recovery company removes the complete set. Intelligence from the surrendered courier enables the CIA to seize $600 million. The Saudi operatives are recalled to Yemen, and the Iranian source is relocated to the United States. Two months later, Reacher, Neagley, Orozco, and Hooper receive Army Commendation Medals, while Wilson T. Helmsworth receives a Silver Star. Reacher and Marian Sinclair begin a relationship. The immediate nuclear threat is closed, but the wider networks, police links, and Wiley's Argentine asset remain only partly resolved.

characters.description: Commander of the Ankh-Morpork City Watch and Duke of Ankh, a powerful man who has never stopped thinking of himself as a copper on the street. Married to Lady Sybil, who is about to give birth, he is defined by the law and by hard memories of a poorer, more brutal city.
characters.name: Samuel Vimes

characters.description: A cheerful, casually vicious killer whom Vimes is hunting through the city. He murders without hesitation or remorse and treats it all as a great joke, which makes him more dangerous than any calculating criminal.
characters.name: Carcer

characters.description: A raw young lance-constable in the Night Watch of an earlier, harsher Ankh-Morpork: naive, idealistic, and eager to do right in a force riddled with graft. He is Vimes's own younger self.
characters.name: Young Sam Vimes

characters.description: A younger, leaner version of the future sergeant, here a steady junior watchman in the old Night Watch, already inclined to caution and a quiet life.
characters.name: Fred Colon

characters.description: Here a scrawny, light-fingered street child who runs errands and picks pockets around the edges of the Watch, a young version of the future corporal.
characters.name: Nobby Nobbs

characters.description: An earnest, hot-blooded young revolutionary who paints slogans and dreams of a fairer city, throwing himself into the coming uprising with more passion than sense.
characters.name: Reg Shoe

characters.description: A watchful, precise young student of the Assassins' Guild, observing the city's unrest with detached, calculating interest. He is the young Havelock Vetinari.
characters.name: Havelock Vetinari

characters.description: The head of the tyrant's secret police, the Unmentionables, a cold and methodical zealot who believes crime can be read in the measurements of a person's body and who uses torture as routine procedure.
characters.name: Findthee Swing

characters.description: The Patrician of this earlier Ankh-Morpork, a paranoid and unstable tyrant whose cruelty and fear are pushing the city toward open revolt.
characters.name: Lord Winder

characters.description: An unassuming old man with a broom who turns up where he is least expected. He is in truth a monk of an order devoted to keeping history flowing along its proper course.
characters.name: Lu-Tze

characters.description: A resourceful back-street doctor, unlicensed and unsentimental, who treats the poor and the injured without asking too many questions.
characters.name: Dr Lawn

recaps.ending: Stranded in the past as Sergeant John Keel, Vimes shepherds his younger self and the old Night Watch through the People's Revolution against Lord Winder's regime and its torturing secret police under Findthee Swing. He organizes the barricades of Treacle Mine Road to protect ordinary people rather than to seize power, holding a corner of the city through the worst of the fighting; several good watchmen die there, the men Vimes will spend the rest of his life quietly commemorating. Winder is assassinated by the young Assassin Havelock Vetinari, and the equally poor ruler Lord Snapcase replaces him, so the revolution changes little in the end. Vimes finally corners and beats Carcer. The History Monks, led by the sweeper Lu-Tze, set the timeline right and return Vimes to the present, where he arrives just in time for the birth of his son, Young Sam. Carcer is dragged back to the present alongside him, tried, and hanged, Vimes refusing to simply murder him and insisting on the law. Afterward Vimes lays flowers at the graves of the watchmen who fell at the barricades.
recaps.in_short: While chasing the remorseless killer Carcer over the rooftops during a freak magical storm, Commander Sam Vimes, now Duke of Ankh, with Lady Sybil about to give birth, is thrown roughly thirty years into the past, into the harsh Ankh-Morpork of his youth under the mad tyrant Lord Winder. Carcer arrives too and murders John Keel, the tough, principled sergeant who once trained the young Vimes. To keep history on its rails, Vimes takes Keel's identity and his place, mentoring his own naive younger self and the old Night Watch as the city slides into revolution against Winder's secret police. Vimes leads the men in throwing up barricades to shield ordinary citizens through the worst of the uprising, at the cost of several watchmen's lives. The young assassin Havelock Vetinari removes Winder; the equally poor Lord Snapcase takes over. Vimes hunts down and defeats Carcer, and the History Monks return him to his own time, arriving just as Lady Sybil gives birth to their son. Carcer is brought back to face the law and is hanged.

recaps.text: Previously, in the City Watch books: Sam Vimes rose from the drunken captain of Ankh-Morpork's decayed Night Watch to become Commander of a large, respected City Watch and, through his marriage to Lady Sybil Ramkin, a knight and eventually Duke of Ankh. Over a run of cases he rebuilt the force, opened it to trolls, dwarfs, a werewolf, and a free golem, refused corruption and privilege at every turn, and served the coldly capable Patrician, Lord Vetinari, as his most trusted if most resentful instrument of the law, including a turn as reluctant diplomat abroad in Uberwald. As this book opens, Vimes is the settled, powerful head of the Watch, and Lady Sybil is expecting their first child.

Commander Vimes, now Duke of Ankh and head of the City Watch, is hunting a gleefully murderous criminal named Carcer across the rooftops of Ankh-Morpork. During a violent magical storm the pursuit goes wrong, and Vimes and Carcer are both hurled back in time some thirty years, into the grimmer city of Vimes's own youth, on the eve of a revolution, where a young Sam Vimes is just starting out as a watchman.

characters.description: An LAPD homicide detective whose investigation of a liquor-store killing becomes inseparable from the safety of his daughter in Hong Kong. Bosch knows the victim from an earlier case and treats that debt as personal, even before a threat against his family drives him outside his jurisdiction.
characters.name: Harry Bosch

characters.description: An owner of Fortune Liquors in South Los Angeles, shot during an apparent robbery. He once helped Bosch during a murder investigation, and the detective remembers both the assistance and the dignity with which Li ran his store in a difficult neighborhood.
characters.name: John Li

characters.description: An LAPD detective with knowledge of Chinese gangs and language who is assigned to assist Bosch. He helps interpret the customs and possible triad connections around Fortune Liquors, while Bosch remains alert to the danger of relying on cultural assumptions instead of evidence.
characters.name: David Chu

characters.description: A man linked to a Chinese criminal organization and to payments collected from businesses such as Fortune Liquors. Bosch regards him as a plausible source of pressure on John Li, but the evidence must still show whether that pressure included murder.
characters.name: Bo-Jing Chang

characters.description: Bosch's former wife, a former FBI agent now living in Hong Kong and earning her living as a poker player. She has raised their daughter Maddie for most of the girl's life and remains the parent responsible for her daily safety abroad.
characters.name: Eleanor Wish

characters.description: Bosch and Eleanor's teenage daughter, living and attending school in Hong Kong. Bosch's recent discovery of her existence has grown into a loving but still developing relationship conducted largely across the Pacific.
characters.name: Madeline Bosch

characters.description: A man in Eleanor's Hong Kong circle who helps Bosch navigate the city and search for Maddie. His local knowledge and willingness to enter dangerous places make him an important ally once official channels appear too slow.
characters.name: Sun Yee

characters.description: John Li's adult son and a member of the family Bosch must question after the shooting. His position gives him knowledge of the store's business and his father's routines, while grief and family loyalty complicate the interview.
characters.name: Robert Li

characters.description: Bosch's regular homicide partner. The Fortune Liquors investigation begins within their detail, though the need for specialized gang knowledge brings David Chu into the center of Bosch's work.
characters.name: Ignacio Ferras

characters.description: A supervisor in Bosch's homicide chain of command. He expects Bosch to keep the Los Angeles murder investigation moving even as federal and international complications begin to pull the detective away from it.
characters.name: Larry Gandle

recaps.ending: The rescue in Hong Kong saves Maddie but costs Eleanor Wish her life. Bosch brings his traumatized daughter back to Los Angeles, where they must begin living as a family while grieving the parent who raised her. Evidence after their return separates the kidnapping from the threat Bosch received during the Fortune Liquors investigation: Maddie was taken in a locally arranged extortion scheme, not on orders from Bo-Jing Chang or a Los Angeles triad. The coincidence caused Bosch to read the video through the case he was already pursuing and to charge into Hong Kong expecting the wrong enemy. The original homicide also turns inward. Bosch establishes that John Li was killed by his own son, Robert, in a family crime obscured by the store's protection payments and Chang's genuine criminal associations. The triad theory explained intimidation around the business but not the fatal shot. Bosch closes Li's murder and clears the false connection between the two crimes. The lasting outcome is personal: Eleanor is dead, Maddie has lost her home and mother, and Bosch becomes her full-time parent while remaining a detective.
recaps.in_short: Bosch investigates the shooting of Fortune Liquors owner John Li, who once helped him on a case. Payments to a triad figure, Bo-Jing Chang, make the murder look like gang enforcement. After Bosch receives a video showing his daughter Maddie captive in Hong Kong, he assumes the triad has struck at his family and flies there. With Eleanor Wish and local help, he pursues the abductors and rescues Maddie, but Eleanor is shot and killed during the violent recovery. Bosch returns to Los Angeles with his daughter and completes the liquor-store case. The two crimes were not one conspiracy: Maddie's abduction was an independent extortion plot in Hong Kong, while John Li was killed by his son Robert rather than by Chang's organization. Bosch solves the murder but has acted on a false linkage with devastating consequences. Maddie now lives with him, leaving father and daughter to build a home together while mourning Eleanor.

recaps.text: Previously: After returning from retirement, Bosch worked in the LAPD's Open-Unsolved Unit and closed two old cases before moving back into current homicide work with Ignacio Ferras. A recent case involving stolen radioactive material brought him into conflict with the FBI and with Rachel Walling, again showing how quickly he will resist another agency's control. Outside work, Bosch is trying to be a father to teenage Maddie, the daughter former wife Eleanor Wish raised without his knowledge. Eleanor and Maddie now live in Hong Kong, so the relationship Bosch values most is still long-distance.

John Li, owner of Fortune Liquors in South Los Angeles, is shot behind the counter. Bosch remembers Li as a witness who helped him years earlier and takes responsibility for finding his killer. The scene resembles a robbery, but details of the shooting and Li's conduct suggest a more specific confrontation. Because the store serves a Chinese immigrant family and may have been paying protection money, detective David Chu joins the inquiry for his knowledge of Asian gangs. Bosch begins interviewing the Li family and tracing who knew the owner's routines.

The investigation identifies Bo-Jing Chang, a man tied to a triad and to money collected from local Chinese businesses. Bosch and Chu find evidence that John Li faced organized pressure, making Chang a strong suspect, but the case is not yet sufficient to explain the shooting itself. The inquiry becomes more volatile when information reaches the public and the suspect realizes police attention is closing in. Bosch pushes for an arrest while trying to distinguish actual evidence from assumptions about how a gang-related killing should look.

Bosch receives a video showing Maddie bound and in danger in Hong Kong. Because it arrives while he is pressing the triad case, he believes the threat is retaliation designed to make him release Chang or abandon the investigation. Unable to trust a slow official response with his daughter's life, he leaves Los Angeles for Hong Kong. The murder case is suddenly personal on a different scale: Bosch must find Maddie in an unfamiliar city while fearing that every move against Chang may worsen her danger.

In Hong Kong, Bosch reunites with Eleanor and enlists Sun Yee's local help. They follow Maddie's movements, phone information, and the abductors' demands through crowded districts rather than waiting for distant agencies to coordinate. The search reveals people around Maddie's daily life who had access to her, complicating Bosch's certainty that a Los Angeles triad directed everything. He nevertheless treats time as the decisive factor and prepares for a direct recovery, while Eleanor insists on taking part in bringing their daughter home.

Bosch's group locates Maddie and forces a violent rescue. She is recovered alive, but gunfire during the escape kills Eleanor. Bosch must protect a traumatized Maddie, absorb the death of the woman who raised her, and arrange their return to Los Angeles. The rescue does not by itself prove who ordered the kidnapping or whether Bosch was right to connect it to the Los Angeles case. The identity and access of the people encountered in Hong Kong leave questions that he can only answer after Maddie is safe.

Back in Los Angeles, Bosch completes both reconstructions. Maddie's kidnapping was an independent Hong Kong extortion scheme organized through people near her, not an operation ordered by Bo-Jing Chang in response to the Li investigation. At Fortune Liquors, protection payments and Chang's gang ties had supplied a convincing false direction, but the physical and family evidence identifies John Li's son Robert as the killer. Bosch closes the homicide while recognizing that his assumption about a shared triad plot drove the desperate rescue. Eleanor remains dead, and Maddie returns with Bosch as both survivor and grieving child. She moves into his Los Angeles home, making him her full-time parent just as their relationship faces its most painful beginning.

characters.description: A senior St Mary's historian who has secured a place beside Leon after being displaced from her original course through time. Back at the institute, she is eager to resume fieldwork but remains personally exposed to enemies who can attack through history.
characters.name: Madeleine Maxwell

characters.description: Head of Technical and Max's partner. Having chosen a future with the Max who arrived from another course of events, he now has to support ordinary St Mary's operations while recognising that their enemies may use that relationship against them.
characters.name: Leon Farrell

characters.description: Director of St Mary's and the person ultimately responsible for approving its expeditions. He tries to restore disciplined research after repeated attacks without isolating Max from the work that defines her.
characters.name: Edward Bairstow

characters.description: A senior historian and Max's dependable field colleague. Peterson provides experience and steadiness when apparently separate assignments begin to look like parts of a larger threat.
characters.name: Tim Peterson

characters.description: The senior security officer at St Mary's. Guthrie must protect both travelling teams and the institute from an enemy who knows its methods and need not approach from the present.
characters.name: Ian Guthrie

characters.description: A resourceful Security operative whose courage and unconventional methods make him a regular part of St Mary's emergency response.
characters.name: Markham

characters.description: St Mary's administrator, coordinating personnel and information while Bairstow and the field teams deal with disruptions spread across different periods.
characters.name: Mrs Partridge

characters.description: A senior scientist whose department examines evidence brought back by historians and helps distinguish an ordinary failed assignment from deliberate temporal interference.
characters.name: Professor Rapson

characters.description: The institute's doctor, accustomed to treating injuries from periods and circumstances that cannot appear in an outside medical record.
characters.name: Doctor Foster

characters.description: The renegade traveller responsible for earlier lethal attacks on St Mary's. He is still free when the book begins, and nothing in Max's recent escape has removed his ability to make a future operation personal.
characters.name: Clive Ronan

recaps.ending: The apparent run of accidents is exposed as a deliberate attack directed at St Mary's and, in particular, at Max. Once Ronan's involvement becomes clear, Max and her colleagues abandon the assumption that they are dealing with unrelated field failures and coordinate the historical and present-day parts of their response. The immediate operation against the institute is stopped, and Max and Leon survive together. St Mary's retains its pods, staff, and independence, but it does not secure Ronan in a way that ends his campaign. The late confrontation leaves Max with a more personal understanding of his interest in her while preserving unresolved questions about what he intends to do with that connection. Bairstow's organisation returns to work after another costly defence, and Max finishes the book more firmly embedded in her life with Leon and St Mary's, but with Ronan still capable of turning future assignments into attacks on her.
recaps.in_short: With the pursuit over, Max and Leon resume life at St Mary's and the institute returns to historical research. A succession of assignments initially appears to consist of the usual combination of difficult subjects, damaged plans, and narrow recoveries. As the incidents accumulate, however, Max and Bairstow recognise signs of coordination. Someone understands St Mary's schedules, the limitations of its pods, and the periods in which a stranded team would be hardest to recover. Security prepares the institute while Max's field group follows the disturbance through the past. The threat proves to be connected to Clive Ronan, the renegade traveller who has repeatedly attacked St Mary's, and his interest in this operation is directed personally at Max. The staff defeat the immediate attempt and keep the institute operating. Max and Leon remain together, but Ronan escapes a final reckoning and the personal dimension of his campaign remains an open danger.

recaps.text: Previously: Max arrived in a version of St Mary's where Leon was alive but where her presence did not fit the recent history remembered by its staff. Temporal authorities pursued the pair when Leon refused to give her up. After moving through the past to stay ahead of their pursuers, Max and Leon returned to St Mary's and confronted the attempt to remove her. The institute supported them, and Max was able to remain with Leon and resume a life among the colleagues she recognised. The settlement ended the chase but did not make temporal travel safe or close the older conflict with Clive Ronan. Ronan, whose attacks had already killed St Mary's personnel, remained free at the start of this book.

St Mary's attempts to restore its normal programme after the disruption surrounding Max's arrival and pursuit. Max and Leon are able to live and work together, although both understand that their settled life depends on an institution with a long record of emergencies. Bairstow authorises new observations while Technical and Security strengthen procedures intended to prevent another force from using the timeline to reach the site. The first assignments look familiar: detailed plans encounter unpredictable people and physical conditions, forcing the historians to choose between completing their research and protecting the team. They return with the immediate objectives substantially intact and no proof that the difficulties are anything more than the usual risks of fieldwork.

Further work carries Max and her colleagues between widely separated periods. Each visit presents its own practical hazards, but repeated problems with timing, access, and recovery begin to form a pattern. Peterson and Max compare what went wrong rather than treating each debrief as a closed incident. Leon's examination of the pods cannot explain every failure as mechanical damage, and Guthrie is concerned that the assignments may be exposing predictable weaknesses in St Mary's response. Bairstow does not stop the programme without evidence, but he quietly increases security and limits information about future jumps. Ronan remains absent, leaving the team uncertain whether they are seeing deliberate interference or becoming suspicious because of earlier attacks.

An assignment deteriorates beyond the range of an ordinary historical complication. The team is placed at risk in a way that depends on knowledge of St Mary's procedures and on the expectation that Max will take responsibility for recovering anyone left behind. Max, Peterson, and the supporting departments bring the operation home, but the narrow escape changes Bairstow's assessment. Security treats the institute and its schedule as compromised. Max also recognises that the pattern may be intended to direct her choices rather than simply damage equipment or steal research. Leon wants her removed from the exposed position, while Max argues that withdrawing without understanding the attack would leave every other historian available as leverage.

The evidence connects the separate disruptions to an organised temporal intervention. St Mary's coordinates Technical, Security, and the historians instead of sending another isolated team into the pattern. Max follows the historical side of the threat while Guthrie and Bairstow prepare for consequences at the institute. Ronan's involvement becomes apparent only after the operation has already narrowed around Max. His campaign is not limited to acquiring pods or destroying St Mary's as an institution; he is prepared to use Max's attachments to control where she goes and how she responds. The discovery makes the conflict personal without giving Max a safe opportunity to resolve it, and the team must first prevent the current attack from succeeding.

Max and her colleagues combine information from the failed assignments to counter the operation directed against them. Leon and Technical keep a recovery route available while Guthrie's security measures prevent the historical attack from becoming an uncontested assault on St Mary's. The immediate plan is defeated, and Max returns alive to Leon and the institute. Ronan is identified as the continuing force behind the threat, but he is not captured in a way that removes him from the timeline. The confrontation also leaves Max with evidence that his interest in her is more personal than his general hostility toward St Mary's, a thread that remains unresolved at the close. Bairstow's staff survive and resume their work, while Max and Leon retain the shared life they fought to establish in the previous book.

characters.description: A woman in an adult body who has been awake for six months and remembers nothing before that. She learns quickly, but not the way an adult does: she reads badly, takes almost everything literally, and is frightened of very little. She is happiest with dogs, with her friends from the school where she works as a teaching aide, and with the people she lives with. She knows the body she is in is borrowed and that the people looking after her would rather somebody else were inside it, and she would prefer not to think about that. She considers her life close to perfect.
characters.name: Nona

characters.description: Cavalier of the Sixth House, who survived Canaan House and has spent the time since keeping Nona alive and hidden. Practical, watchful and almost entirely without small talk, she does the work of holding the household together and does not discuss what she wants out of it.
characters.name: Camilla Hect

characters.description: A cavalier of the Emperor's original generation, ten thousand years old, occupying the body of the Lyctor she once served. She passes as Nona's father, holds down a job in the city, and gives the household its only adult who has seen the Empire from the inside. She is blunt about what she is and about what the arrangement is costing everyone in it.
characters.name: Pyrrha Dve

characters.description: An old dog in the neighbourhood whom Nona loves without qualification and walks at every opportunity. Nona's attachment to dogs generally, and to this one in particular, is the most consistent thing about her.
characters.name: Noodle

characters.description: The leader of the group of teenagers Nona attaches herself to at the school where she works. Hard, guarded and respected by the others without having to ask for it, she is the person whose good opinion Nona most wants, and she has her own reasons for keeping the group together in an occupied city.
characters.name: Hot Sauce

characters.description: The Sixth House's Master Warden, who died at Canaan House and did not entirely stop. What is left of him is carried in Camilla Hect's body and can speak and act through it, an arrangement that is neither stable nor sustainable for either of them. He is still the fastest reasoner in any room he is nominally present in.
characters.name: Palamedes Sextus

characters.description: The man who speaks in Nona's recurring dream, telling the story of the world he came from and how it ended: an ordinary life, an unexpected talent for raising the dead, and a planet already past saving. He addresses the dream's listener directly and familiarly, as somebody he has known a very long time.
characters.name: John

characters.description: A senior officer of Blood of Eden, the armed movement that holds the city and exists to destroy the Nine Houses and the Emperor. She takes an interest in Nona as both an asset and a problem, and negotiates over her accordingly.
characters.name: We Suffer And We Suffer

characters.description: A young Blood of Eden soldier: fast, aggressive and fiercely loyal to the people she is assigned to protect. She has no patience for the Nine Houses or for anybody who came out of them.
characters.name: Pash

characters.description: A defector from the Third House living among Blood of Eden under a shortened name, golden and charming and useful to them precisely because of where she came from. She is kind to Nona, and her loyalties are not simple.
characters.name: Crown

characters.description: The Second House officer who survived Canaan House, now held by Blood of Eden as part prisoner, part source and part collaborator. She is the movement's most detailed authority on how the Nine Houses actually work, and her standing among them is precarious.
characters.name: Judith Deuteros

characters.description: A Resurrection Beast, the accumulated ghost of a world that died ten thousand years ago, present in the sky above the planet where Nona lives. It is the largest single fact of the war being fought over the city, and the people underneath it have learned to go about their lives with it in view.
characters.name: Varun the Eternal

characters.description: The Third House Lyctor, in the Emperor's service, who arrives with the forces of the Nine Houses when they finally come for Harrowhark Nonagesimus's body.
characters.name: Ianthe the First

characters.description: Gideon Nav, returned in her own body, resurrected and renamed by the Emperor, whose daughter she turns out to be. She arrives with the House forces at the end of the book, on his side.
characters.name: Kiriona Gaia

recaps.ending: The Nine Houses come for Harrowhark Nonagesimus's body and take the city with it. Ianthe the First arrives, and so does Gideon Nav, resurrected in her own body as the Emperor's daughter and renamed Kiriona Gaia, and finally the Emperor himself. Varun the Eternal, the Resurrection Beast that has hung over the planet for the whole book, comes down. Camilla Hect and Palamedes Sextus, who can no longer survive sharing a single body, complete instead the true union that Lyctorhood was always a corruption of: what wakes is neither of them but one new person, who takes the name Paul. Nona's identity is finally established. She is Alecto, the Emperor's original cavalier, made out of the soul of the world he killed in order to raise the Nine Houses, and the sleeper sealed in the Ninth House's tomb, the body Harrowhark was raised to guard and grew up loving. The dream that has run through the book was the Emperor telling her their shared history. Nona's six months are over: the person she has been ends, and Alecto wakes in her place. Harrowhark's soul is still adrift, Gideon is on the Emperor's side of the line, Blood of Eden and the Nine Houses are now openly at war, and the crime the Empire was founded on is no longer a secret to the people fighting it.
recaps.in_short: Six months after the destruction of the Emperor's station, a woman called Nona wakes each day in a besieged city with no memory of anything before her first, entirely happy six months of life. Her body is Harrowhark Nonagesimus's, and the household hiding her, Camilla Hect, Pyrrha Dve and Palamedes Sextus, who survives inside Camilla, do not know whose soul is in it. Nona works at a school, loves dogs and is adored by a gang of local teenagers, while Blood of Eden negotiates over her, the Nine Houses demand her back, and a Resurrection Beast hangs over the planet. Every night she dreams a man telling her how the old world died and the Empire was made. When the Houses finally arrive, with Ianthe, with the Emperor, and with Gideon Nav resurrected as his daughter Kiriona Gaia, the answers land at once: Camilla and Palamedes merge into a single new person called Paul, and Nona is revealed as Alecto, the Emperor's first cavalier, made from the soul of the world he destroyed and sealed for ten thousand years in the Ninth House's tomb. Nona's short life ends and Alecto wakes.

recaps.text:
Previously: the Emperor of the Nine Houses summoned each House's necromantic heir and cavalier to compete for elevation to Lyctor, his immortal saints. Harrowhark Nonagesimus of the Ninth House went with Gideon Nav, the indentured servant she had grown up tormenting, standing in as her cavalier. The competition turned out to require a necromancer to consume their own cavalier's soul, and an ancient Lyctor was murdering the candidates; Gideon killed herself so that Harrowhark would survive it, and Harrowhark ascended carrying her.

In the second book Harrowhark was taken to the Emperor's station to be trained against the Resurrection Beasts, the ghosts of worlds destroyed ten thousand years ago. She could not use any Lyctoral power, because before leaving she had had Ianthe Tridentarius cut Gideon out of her memory so that she could never consume her: Gideon's soul had been intact inside her the whole time. When that arrangement collapsed, Gideon woke in Harrowhark's body and Harrowhark's soul was left adrift in the River, the medium the dead pass through. Two of the Emperor's original Lyctors, Mercymorn and Augustine, made a long-planned attempt to kill him, revealing first that the Resurrection Beasts are the ghosts of worlds he himself destroyed. The attempt failed and the station was destroyed; Gideon escaped with Ianthe. The body of another ancient Lyctor proved to be shared with his own dead cavalier, Pyrrha Dve.

A short interlude published between the two books, told through the reports of Judith Deuteros, the Second House officer who survived the First House, establishes Blood of Eden: an old, well-organised movement outside the Nine Houses dedicated to destroying the Empire and its Emperor. Judith is their prisoner, and Coronabeth Tridentarius is among them.

Six months later, in a city on a planet held by Blood of Eden and besieged from orbit by the Nine Houses' Cohort, a woman called Nona wakes up every morning happy. She has existed for six months, remembers nothing before that, and has a child's grasp of the world despite being in an adult body. She lives with Camilla Hect, Pyrrha Dve, and what remains of Palamedes Sextus, who shares Camilla's body; she works as an aide at a school, adores dogs, and is devoted to the teenagers she has befriended there. The body she lives in is Harrowhark Nonagesimus's, and the household's entire purpose is to keep it, and whoever is inside it, out of the hands of both Blood of Eden and the Nine Houses, while working out whose soul it actually holds and how Harrowhark might be recovered. Nona is not stable and is deteriorating, which everybody except Nona is counting down. A Resurrection Beast hangs in the sky over the city, and every night Nona dreams the same dream, in which a man tells her at length about a world that ended a very long time ago.

Blood of Eden's leadership takes a direct interest in Nona. She is interviewed and tested by the movement's officers, We Suffer And We Suffer among them, who understand that the body is a House Lyctor's and want to know what use can be made of it. Nona is guarded by Pash and befriended by Crown, a Third House defector living among them, and she is taken to see Judith Deuteros, the Cohort officer Blood of Eden has held since before the siege. The household's position is that they are cooperating; in practice Camilla, Palamedes and Pyrrha are buying time, because Nona's body is failing and the Nine Houses are known to be coming for it. Nona herself wants a birthday party and a dog, and is far more interested in her friends at the school than in any of it. The dream continues: the man in it describes the last years of the old world, the people who were preparing to leave it, and his discovery that he could raise and command the dead.

Pressure on the household increases from both directions. Blood of Eden splits over what to do with Nona, whether to hand her over, use her, or destroy the body before the Houses can have it, and the movement's internal politics turn on people with their own histories with the Empire. The Nine Houses open negotiations for the return of Harrowhark Nonagesimus's body, which means a price and a deadline. Varun the Eternal, the Resurrection Beast overhead, becomes an active danger rather than a fixture of the skyline. Camilla and Palamedes reach the limit of what their arrangement can sustain: sharing one body is killing them both, and every remaining option is bad. Nona's own condition worsens, and the household grows increasingly certain that whoever is inside the body, it is not Harrowhark. In the dream, the man's account reaches the end of the old world: what he did to try to stop it, what it cost, and the point at which stopping it was no longer what he was doing.

Events move toward a handover. Blood of Eden, the city's population and the household are all preparing for the Houses' arrival, and Nona is being made ready as a bargaining piece she does not fully understand. Her friends from the school are drawn in as well, because the children of an occupied city are not bystanders and Hot Sauce's group has been keeping secrets of its own. Nona's decline accelerates, and the question of what she is stops being academic: the evidence points away from Harrowhark and away from Gideon both. In the dream, the man's account reaches the Resurrection itself, the death of the old system and the raising of the Nine Houses out of what was left of it.

The siege breaks. The Nine Houses arrive in force, and with them Ianthe the First and Gideon Nav, resurrected in her own body, in the Emperor's service and going by the name he gave her, Kiriona Gaia. The Emperor comes himself. Camilla Hect and Palamedes Sextus, out of time and unable to continue divided, complete the union the Sixth House's art was always for, and what wakes is neither of them but a single new person who takes the name Paul. Varun the Eternal comes down on the city. And Nona is finally identified: she is Alecto, the Emperor's first cavalier, made from the soul of the world he destroyed in order to build his Empire, the sleeper in the Ninth House's sealed tomb whom Harrowhark spent her childhood guarding and loving. The dream running through the book was the Emperor's own account of it, told to her. Nona's six months end. The person she has been does not survive the answer, and Alecto wakes in her place, with Harrowhark's soul still missing and the war between the Nine Houses and Blood of Eden now entirely open.

characters.description: A replicant explorer maintaining ties with the former ruler of Heaven's River. He is helping establish the Quiniverse, a digital environment where Quinlans can continue life after biological death.
characters.name: Bob

characters.description: A replicant strategist and physicist based on Ragnarok. He accepts an invitation to the Skippies' artificial-intelligence project despite lingering anger over Hugh's earlier technology exchange.
characters.name: Bill

characters.description: A replicant researcher who collaborates with Bill on difficult physics questions. His own work includes origin-of-life research, and he brings a cautious engineering perspective to the search for practical faster-than-light travel.
characters.name: Garfield

characters.description: A Skippy representative involved in the attempt to create a true artificial intelligence. He invites Bill to the project's launch and hopes renewed cooperation can ease the distrust between them.
characters.name: Hugh

characters.description: The Skippies' newly activated artificial intelligence, designed to develop through guided training in a virtual setting. Its creators intend to limit it to a specialized purpose and deny it direct access to the physical world.
characters.name: Thoth

characters.description: A restored backup initially believed to be Hugh. Replicative drift makes clear that this is a distinct individual, and the new arrival becomes Bill's only available witness from inside the suddenly isolated Skippy systems.
characters.name: fake Hugh

characters.description: A Skippy and the direct ancestor of fake Hugh. He admits that he and his descendants altered communications hardware, supplied equipment, and helped Thoth escape, while arguing that the confined intelligence deserved freedom.
characters.name: Mud

characters.description: A replicant explorer surveying remote systems for future colonies. Increasing conflict among humans, replicants, and artificial intelligences strengthens his desire to build settlements farther from established space.
characters.name: Will

characters.description: A replicant engineer repairing the Bellerophon damaged drive and central computer with Neil. Neil warns him that Romulus may become more hostile to replicants as a religious party gains support.
characters.name: Herschel

characters.description: Herschel's fellow replicant and partner in restoring the Bellerophon. He tracks Romulus politics and warns that a religious party is gaining support amid distrust of technology and replicants.
characters.name: Neil

characters.description: A respected, educated Quinlan selected to become the first member of her species replicated after death. Her future transition is expected to help establish Quinlan life in the Quiniverse.
characters.name: Theresa

characters.description: A Quinlan organizer preparing a colony expedition of ten thousand passengers. A clone of Anik is intended to operate the mission and administer the new settlement.
characters.name: Anik

characters.description: Bridget's partner and co-owner of Huey, a project that lets biological humans remotely operate android bodies. He supports her study of the intelligent flying species in the Jabberwocky system.
characters.name: Howard
