Cooper is open about his relationship with Kris and keeps his prospects in baseball; Addy has a life of her own and a real relationship with Ashton; Bronwyn and Nate stay together as she leaves for Yale. The four end the year knowing exactly what was done to them and that the person who did it is beyond any consequence.

characters.description: Bronwyn Rojas's younger sister, now a Bayview High student in her own right and twice a survivor of childhood leukemia. Everyone who knows her history handles her carefully, which she resents. Sharp and habitually secretive, she is the person the older Bayview crew still call when something needs to be found online, and she keeps her own worries strictly to herself.
characters.name: Maeve Rojas

characters.description: Maeve's closest friend and, briefly, her boyfriend, an easygoing Bayview student who interns at Until Proven, the legal nonprofit that defended Nate Macauley. Self-deprecating to the point of treating himself as the least interesting person in any room, he is less certain of what he wants than he lets anyone see.
characters.name: Knox Myers

characters.description: A Bayview student who has learned to keep her distance from the school's social machinery. Her family has been unsteady since her father's death, and she works and covers at home more than her classmates realize. She has an older sister, Emma, and a younger brother, Owen.
characters.name: Phoebe Lawton

characters.description: Phoebe's older sister, a year ahead of her at Bayview and known for being unshakeable: top of her class, calm under pressure, and the member of the family everyone has leaned on since their father died. She and Phoebe have grown apart without either of them saying so.
characters.name: Emma Lawton

characters.description: The youngest of the Lawton children, a middle schooler who spends most of his time gaming and is kept outside whatever his sisters are dealing with.
characters.name: Owen Lawton

characters.description: A popular Bayview athlete, loud and accustomed to getting away with things, near the centre of his year's social group.
characters.name: Brandon Weber

characters.description: A Bayview senior whose family runs Cafe Contigo, the restaurant that has become the crew's second home. Warm, unflappable and a genuinely steady friend, he works shifts alongside Nate Macauley and has known Maeve for years.
characters.name: Luis Santos

characters.description: Maeve's older sister, one of the Bayview Four, now at Yale and still trying to manage her family from several states away. Her relationship with Nate has become long distance and is under strain.
characters.name: Bronwyn Rojas

characters.description: One of the Bayview Four, finished with school and working at Cafe Contigo. He is still the first person Bayview reaches for when it wants a suspect, and he is trying to hold together a relationship with Bronwyn while she is away.
characters.name: Nate Macauley

characters.description: One of the Bayview Four, living with her sister Ashton and working while she decides what she wants next. Confident in a way she was not before Simon Kelleher's death, she becomes a protective older presence for the younger students caught up in the new trouble.
characters.name: Addy Prentiss

characters.description: The lawyer at Until Proven who defended Nate Macauley and now keeps Knox on as an intern. Dry, overworked and hard to alarm, he is the adult the group takes things to when they need someone who will act.
characters.name: Eli Kleinfelter

characters.description: Addy's older sister, out of her marriage and rebuilding, who shares a home with Addy and treats the younger Bayview students with the same blunt practicality.
characters.name: Ashton Prentiss

characters.description: One of the Bayview Four, playing professional baseball away from home and open about his relationship with Kris. He stays in touch with the others and follows what is happening in Bayview from a distance.
characters.name: Cooper Clay

recaps.ending: Emma Lawton is revealed to be responsible for Brandon Weber's death. Phoebe's older sister, the member of the family everyone treated as the reliable one, used the anonymous game to arrange a dare that would kill him, and then kept the game running afterwards so that suspicion would keep moving around the school rather than settling on her. The account itself was set up by a Bayview student who had studied what Simon Kelleher did with About That and wanted the same hold over the school; Emma took it over and put it to a different use. Maeve, Knox and Phoebe piece it together from what the account knew and when it could have learned it, and Emma is exposed and taken into custody. Phoebe is left having been the one who worked out what her sister had done, and the Lawtons are left to absorb it. Maeve has stopped hiding her health from her parents, from Bronwyn and from Knox, and she and Luis Santos have become close. Knox has stopped treating himself as the least important person in the room. Bayview has a second dead student and the knowledge that the pattern Simon started can be picked up by anyone who wants it.
recaps.in_short: Eighteen months after Simon Kelleher's death, an anonymous account revives his methods at Bayview High with a game of Truth or Dare run by text: each target is named in public, offered a choice, and exposed if they refuse. Phoebe Lawton is one of the first casualties. Maeve Rojas, whose sister was one of the Bayview Four and who is hiding the possibility that her cancer has returned, and her friend Knox Myers set out to identify the account before it reaches them. The school treats the game as a prank until a dare kills the athlete Brandon Weber and the town faces a second homicide investigation. Working from what the account knew and when it could have known it, the three of them establish that the game was started by a student imitating Simon and then taken over by Phoebe's older sister Emma, who arranged Brandon's death and used the game to cover it. Emma is arrested, Maeve stops hiding her health from her family, and Bayview learns that anyone can pick up where Simon left off.

recaps.text: Eighteen months earlier, five Bayview High students were sent to detention and one of them, Simon Kelleher, died of a deliberately induced allergic reaction. Simon ran About That, a gossip app that traded in classmates' secrets, and each of the four survivors was the subject of a post he had scheduled for the following day. Those four, Bronwyn Rojas, Addy Prentiss, Nate Macauley and Cooper Clay, became national news as the Bayview Four while an anonymous account published the secrets Simon had collected: Bronwyn's cheating on an exam, Addy's infidelity, Nate's dealing, Cooper's relationship with a young man. Nate was arrested and charged. Investigating on their own, with help from Bronwyn's younger sister Maeve, they established that Simon had staged his own death to frame them and to be remembered for it, with help from Addy's boyfriend Jake Riordan, who attacked Addy when she confronted him and was arrested. The four were cleared. Bronwyn is now at Yale and still with Nate, Cooper is playing professional baseball and is open about his relationship with Kris, and Addy lives with her sister Ashton. Bayview has never stopped being the town where it happened.

An anonymous account begins running a game of Truth or Dare at Bayview High. Targets are named where the whole school can see it and given a choice: answer a truth the account already knows, or complete a dare. Refusing means the truth is published anyway. The material is accurate and personal, which tells everyone that whoever is behind it has been collecting information the way Simon Kelleher once did, and Bayview reacts to the echo immediately. Phoebe Lawton is among the first named and refuses, and the account makes good on the threat, which costs her at school and at home. The administration treats the game as a prank to be suppressed and the police have nothing they can act on, so the people taking it seriously are the students it is aimed at. Maeve Rojas and Knox Myers start trying to work out who is running the account, partly because they remember how the last one ended and partly because each of them has something they would rather not see published.

The game keeps going and the school keeps watching. More students take the dare rather than risk the truth, which is what preserves the account's audience and its power, and the dares get harder. Phoebe lives with the aftermath of her own exposure, including at home, where her older sister Emma has held the family together since their father died and is assumed by everyone to be coping. Maeve has been hiding the possibility that her cancer has come back and knows precisely what the account could do with that, so she says nothing to Bronwyn, to her parents or to Knox. Knox, interning at Until Proven, has access to Eli Kleinfelter and to adults who would act if anyone could give them a name, and nobody can. Nate Macauley and Addy Prentiss, who know exactly where this leads, are drawn back in through Maeve. The account has not run out of names.

A dare ends in the death of Brandon Weber. What the school had treated as an ugly game becomes a homicide investigation, and a town that has already been through one student death and the coverage that followed braces for a second. The account does not stop; the game continues while the police work, which keeps suspicion moving around the school and makes it impossible to tell targets from participants. Maeve, Knox and Phoebe, each far closer to the game than the adults realize, begin working through what the account knew about each person and when it could have learned it, on the reasoning that its knowledge is the only real evidence anyone has. Maeve's health can no longer be kept from her family. The Bayview Four are pulled back into the story by a town that assumes anything of this kind must connect to them.

Emma Lawton is revealed to be responsible for Brandon Weber's death. Phoebe's older sister used the anonymous game to arrange a dare that would kill him and then kept it running so that suspicion would keep moving around the school; the account itself had been set up by a Bayview student fascinated by what Simon Kelleher had done, and Emma took it over. Maeve, Knox and Phoebe put it together from the pattern of what the account knew, and Emma is exposed and taken into custody, leaving Phoebe as the person who worked out what her own sister had done and the Lawtons to absorb it. Maeve has stopped hiding her illness from her parents, from Bronwyn and from Knox, and she and Luis Santos have become close. Knox has stopped treating himself as an afterthought. Bayview ends with a second dead student and no confidence that the pattern Simon started will not be picked up again.

characters.description: A former Army military-police major whom accused gunman James Barr demands to see. Military records show that their service overlapped, but the reason for Barr's request is not yet known.
characters.name: Jack Reacher

characters.description: A former Army infantry specialist and Gulf War veteran arrested for the plaza shooting. He denies responsibility, asks for Jack Reacher, and is left comatose with stab wounds and a severe brain injury after an attack by other prisoners.
characters.name: James Barr

characters.description: James Barr's sister and next of kin. She had lived in his house before moving out ahead of the shooting. Convinced that he is innocent, she rejects a defense based only on mitigation and seeks a lawyer willing to test the case.
characters.name: Rosemary Barr

characters.description: A retired police officer and licensed investigator who works for local lawyers. Skilled in tracing people and checking records, he establishes that Barr and Reacher served in the Army during the same period but cannot locate Reacher after his discharge.
characters.name: Franklin

characters.description: Barr's first lawyer, who regards the reported physical case as overwhelming. He concentrates on reducing the consequences rather than proving innocence, leading Rosemary Barr to seek representation more receptive to her brother's denial.
characters.name: David Chapman

characters.description: A newly established defense lawyer retained to represent Barr through his sister. The district attorney's daughter and a witness to part of the plaza attack, she begins by independently checking the evidence and considering a medical defense.
characters.name: Helen Rodin

characters.description: The district attorney prosecuting Barr and Helen Rodin's father. He considers the physical evidence decisive, cites a perfect record in capital cases, and intends to prosecute Barr if the prisoner recovers sufficient brain function.
characters.name: Alex Rodin

characters.description: The homicide detective leading the investigation into the plaza shooting. Regarded by others as reliable, he oversees a case built on physical evidence rather than eyewitness identification and presents the findings against Barr as conclusive.
characters.name: Emerson

characters.description: A local television anchor reporting on the plaza shooting and James Barr's arrest. Her broadcast supplies Reacher with the first public account of the case, prompting him to leave Miami and travel by bus to Indiana.
characters.name: Ann Yanni

characters.description: A surveillance operative who watches Jack Reacher and Helen Rodin after their lunch. He is already familiar with Helen's routine.
characters.name: Grigor Linsky

characters.description: The feared elderly leader to whom Grigor Linsky reports. After learning that Reacher has arrived, he directs continued surveillance and orders an indirect, apparently ordinary act of violence intended to drive Reacher away.
characters.name: Zek

characters.description: A police crime-scene specialist who organizes and explains the extensive case against Barr. His presentation covers video, ballistics, prints, the recovered rifle and minivan, and trace evidence from clothing and footwear.
characters.name: Bellantonio

characters.description: A red-haired auto-parts employee who recognizes that Reacher is using a false name. She approaches him in a bar and helps stage an accusation that provides the pretext for five men to attack him.
characters.name: Sandy

characters.description: A man connected to Sandy whom Jack Reacher seeks while tracing the people involved in the failed bar setup. His part in events is unclear.
characters.name: Jeb Oliver

characters.description: One of Zek's associates, present with the organization's senior members when the missing traffic-cone footage threatens the case against Barr. The group considers how to neutralize Reacher without resorting to an obvious direct attack.
characters.name: Chenko

characters.description: An associate who attends Zek's planning meeting as the group considers how to stop Jack Reacher from pursuing the unexplained traffic-cone evidence without an obvious direct attack.
characters.name: Vladimir

characters.description: A member of Zek's organization assigned to surveillance work. He rotates monitoring duty with Sokolov while the group follows Reacher's investigation and tries to protect the apparently conclusive case against Barr.
characters.name: Raskin

characters.description: A Zek associate assigned to surveillance work. He rotates monitoring duty with Raskin while the organization watches Reacher and responds to the defense team's discovery of a weakness in the evidence against Barr.
characters.name: Sokolov

characters.description: A Pentagon-based JAG brigadier general who was formerly involved with Jack Reacher. The defense subpoenas her, and she is expected to give a deposition.
characters.name: Eileen Hutton

characters.description: Emerson's police colleague, assisting with the investigation of Sandy's death. She joins him at the airport to intercept Reacher after the circumstances of the killing make him a leading suspect.
characters.name: Donna Bianca

characters.description: The auto-parts-store employer of Sandy and Jeb Oliver. He identifies Sandy for Emerson and reports her recent contacts with Jack Reacher and Reacher's search for Jeb, directing police attention toward Reacher.
characters.name: Gary

characters.description: The retired Marine shooting champion who owns James Barr's Kentucky range. He keeps dated customer targets and helps Jack Reacher interpret the records showing that Barr concealed declining accuracy while another shooter disguised expert skill.
characters.name: Kentucky range owner

characters.description: The third person killed in the plaza shooting, identified as a DMV clerical supervisor. Analysis of the firing sequence makes her the probable intended target rather than a random victim.
characters.name: Oline Archer

characters.description: Oline Archer's husband, whom she reported missing two months before the plaza shooting. His disappearance becomes the next lead in Jack Reacher's inquiry.
characters.name: Ted Archer

recaps.ending: Reacher's group attacks Zek's isolated house and rescues Rosemary Barr alive. Helen Rodin survives the diversion, while Sokolov, Vladimir, and Grigor Linsky are killed. Chenko is thrown from a third-floor window, but his condition is not confirmed. Zek remains inside, and Reacher goes back to confront him. James Barr appears unable to have fired the plaza shots and therefore appears to have been framed. Reacher links Oline Archer's death and Ted Archer's disappearance to a corrupt city-contract operation, but that theory is not yet independently proved. Barr's legal fate, the official handling of Sandy's murder, the possible leak from Emerson or Alex Rodin, and the ultimate outcomes of Zek and Chenko all remain open at the close.
recaps.in_short: After five people are shot in a public plaza, accused former Army sniper James Barr denies responsibility and asks for Jack Reacher. Reacher arrives expecting to condemn Barr because of concealed killings in Barr's military past, but flaws in the apparently perfect evidence point to coercion and then to a complete frame-up. Reacher identifies Chenko as the concealed marksman and Oline Archer as the likely intended victim. Oline's missing husband, Ted, had challenged a competitor benefiting from corrupt city contracts, connecting the shooting to Zek's organization. The group murders Sandy to implicate Reacher and abducts Rosemary Barr to control the defense. Reacher, Helen Rodin, Ann Yanni, Franklin, and a retired range owner locate Zek's house. Their assault frees Rosemary and kills several operatives. Chenko's condition and Zek's fate remain unresolved, as do Barr's case, the contract conspiracy, and a possible justice-system leak.

recaps.text: Before this case, Jack Reacher served as an Army military-police major and left the service in 1997.

Five people are killed in a plaza shooting, and the physical evidence points overwhelmingly to former Army infantryman James Barr. Barr denies the charge and insists that Jack Reacher be found, but an attack by other prisoners leaves him comatose. His sister Rosemary rejects the assumption of guilt and hires Helen Rodin, daughter of the district attorney prosecuting the case. Reacher sees the news in Miami and travels to Indiana. He initially tells Helen's team that he has come to help condemn Barr, not clear him. Reacher explains that Barr previously confessed to killing four American soldiers in Kuwait, a case the Army concealed because the victims had themselves committed serious crimes. Barr's denial of the new shooting therefore conflicts sharply with his earlier confession. Grigor Linsky begins watching Reacher and Helen. Although the official evidence still appears decisive, Linsky's employer, Zek, orders an indirect attempt to frighten Reacher away. Sandy helps arrange a bar confrontation, but Reacher defeats the attackers and recognizes that the assault was aimed specifically at him. The need to protect an apparently certain prosecution gives him reason to investigate further.

Reacher finds that the parking garage was a poor firing position and that the evidence was left in an unusually conspicuous trail. He first suspects that Barr was forced to shoot and accept blame, with Rosemary as the likely leverage. A missing piece of video then establishes that someone other than Barr placed a traffic cone used in preparing the garage. Zek's organization recognizes the danger and decides to frame Reacher. Chenko and Vladimir lure Sandy away, kill her, and leave her body at Reacher's former hotel. Emerson treats Reacher as the likely killer, while Donna Bianca helps watch for him. Meanwhile, Helen's questions uncover a gun associate of Barr's named Chenko. The official case against Barr remains strong, but the unexplained cone now provides a concrete path toward another participant. Reacher knows Sandy has been killed and that police are closing in, while Barr's connection to Chenko links the accused man to the same organization monitoring the defense.

At a Kentucky shooting range, Reacher studies retained targets and determines that Barr had disguised worsening performance while Chenko concealed expert ability. Barr's emerging Parkinson's disease convinces Reacher that he could not have made the plaza shots. Reacher reconstructs an impersonation scheme in which a shorter shooter used Barr's van, rifle, clothing, and identifying traces. The firing order suggests that DMV supervisor Oline Archer was the intended victim. Her husband Ted had disappeared after his quarry lost city contracts to an apparently corrupt competitor, and Ted's hidden truck connects his disappearance to Jeb Oliver's barn. Franklin traces the contracts to Specialized Services of Indiana and helps locate Zek's remote house beside its stone plant. Before the team can act, Chenko abducts Rosemary to force testimony against Barr. Ann Yanni supplies Reacher with a false alibi when police arrest him for Sandy's death. Reacher, Helen, Ann, Franklin, and the retired range owner organize a rescue. Helen creates thermal decoys while Reacher enters the house, kills Sokolov, Vladimir, and Grigor Linsky, and throws Chenko from an upper window. He frees Rosemary alive. Chenko's survival is unknown, and Zek remains inside as Reacher returns to confront him. Barr's legal outcome and the wider corruption case remain unresolved.

characters.description: A third-year rider at what is left of Basgiath, bonded to two dragons, wielding lightning, and one of the few people who knows exactly what the war against the venin actually is. She comes into this book grieving her mother, carrying the authority that comes from having been right when the leadership was lying, and holding a secret heavier than any she has kept before: what Xaden became to save her. Physically she is still the most breakable rider in any room, and she still compensates with knowledge, preparation and a refusal to be managed by the people who love her.
characters.name: Violet Sorrengail

characters.description: The heir of Tyrrendor and the leader of the resistance, who channelled power from the earth to keep Violet alive during the battle for Basgiath and became venin doing it. He is fighting to stay himself, concealing what he is from almost everyone, and carrying both a hidden second signet and a hunger that gets harder to refuse the longer the war lasts. His relationship with Violet is now bound up in that concealment, and their dragons' mating bond still keeps them within reach of one another.
characters.name: Xaden Riorson

characters.description: Violet's black morningstartail, among the oldest and most powerful dragons alive, blunt to the point of rudeness and entirely without patience for human hesitation. His mating bond with Sgaeyl and his own long memory of the Vale both shape what Violet is able to do.
characters.name: Tairn

characters.description: Violet's golden dragon, who came out of a long sleep during the battle for Basgiath as something no rider had seen before. She is unlike the other dragons of the Vale in ways the Vale has never explained, and the question of what she actually is, and where the rest of her kind went, is one Violet can no longer put aside.
characters.name: Andarna

characters.description: Xaden's blue daggertail, fast and sharp-tongued, mated to Tairn. She is closer than anyone to what her rider has become and is not inclined to discuss it.
characters.name: Sgaeyl

characters.description: Violet's older brother, a mender and one of the leaders of the resistance based in Aretia, who spent six years officially dead. Protective and habitually controlling, he is now one of the last of Violet's family and one of the people whose caution she most often has to argue past.
characters.name: Brennan Sorrengail

characters.description: Violet's older sister, a serving rider who spent her career defending a border against an enemy she was never told the truth about. She comes into this book having lost her mother and having chosen the resistance over the command structure she was raised in.
characters.name: Mira Sorrengail

characters.description: Violet's closest friend and a rider who has grown into command, steady where Violet is impulsive and one of the few people who will tell her plainly when she is wrong. She now knows everything Violet spent the previous year hiding from her.
characters.name: Rhiannon Matthias

characters.description: A rider in Violet's circle who has kept his sense of humour through two years in which most of his classmates died. Beneath it he is dependable in a fight and quietly aware of how much everyone around him is carrying.
characters.name: Ridoc Gamlyn

characters.description: A rider in Violet's circle, older and more methodical than the rest, who has kept flying and fighting through injuries that would have ended anyone else's career.
characters.name: Sawyer Henrick

characters.description: Violet's oldest friend, whose ability to read recent memories through touch spent a year making him a danger to her. He ends the previous book on the other side of the argument he started on, having seen for himself what the command he trusted was concealing.
characters.name: Dain Aetos

characters.description: A marked rider from Tyrrendor, silver-haired and abrasive, wholly committed to the resistance and long past pretending to be a model cadet. She and Violet have become allies through repeated proof rather than affection.
characters.name: Imogen Cardulo

characters.description: Xaden's closest friend and one of the resistance's most capable fighters, positioned close enough to him to notice things about him that Xaden would rather nobody noticed.
characters.name: Garrick Tavis

characters.description: Xaden's cousin, a rider and a member of the resistance's inner circle from the beginning, with his own standing among the marked riders of Tyrrendor.
characters.name: Bodhi Durran

characters.description: Liam Mairi's younger sister, a rider now rather than the hostile first-year who arrived blaming Violet for her brother's death. She came through the battle for Basgiath and has stopped refusing the people trying to keep her alive.
characters.name: Sloane Mairi

characters.description: A gryphon flier from Poromiel, from a prominent family among the drifts, brought into Basgiath by the alliance and kept there by the war. Proud and combative, with history with Xaden that predates Violet, she has become a working ally rather than a guest under guard.
characters.name: Catriona Cordella

recaps.text: Previously: Violet Sorrengail was raised to be a scribe and ordered into Basgiath War College's Riders Quadrant by her mother, the general commanding it. Physically fragile and expected to die in her first weeks, she survived on preparation rather than strength and bonded two dragons at once, the black morningstartail Tairn and the golden feathertail Andarna, and her signet turned out to be lightning. Tairn's mating bond with Sgaeyl tied her to Xaden Riorson, son of the executed leader of Tyrrendor's separatist rebellion, and their hostility became an alliance and then a relationship. At the border town of Resson she learned that Navarre's leadership has spent a century lying: the venin, dark wielders who drain the life out of the land, are real, the wards protecting the kingdom are failing, villages have been abandoned in secret, and Xaden's marked riders have been arming Poromiel against them from the rebel city of Aretia, where Violet's brother Brennan turned out to be alive. Her second year was spent hiding all of that inside a school run by an interrogator, raising new wards for Tyrrendor, arming it with weapons that can kill venin, and building a real alliance with Poromiel's gryphon fliers. It ended with the wards at Basgiath failing and the venin attacking the college outright: the school was devastated, General Lilith Sorrengail died holding the line, Andarna woke from a long sleep as something no rider had seen before, and Xaden saved Violet by drawing power from the earth the way the venin do, becoming venin himself and concealing it.

aliases: the Wicked Witch of the West
characters.description: The green-skinned woman remembered across Oz as the Wicked Witch of the West, long dead when this book opens. Her book of magic, the Grimmerie, her broom and her surviving descendants are still being hunted by both governments now fighting over Oz, which is why her family cannot live openly.
characters.name: Elphaba

characters.description: The girl from another world, older now, whose two previous visits to Oz left two dead Witches behind her. A natural disaster in her own country pitches her back into Oz for a third time, still cheerfully certain of her own innocence and still, to most Ozians, the most notorious foreigner alive.
characters.name: Dorothy

characters.description: A green-skinned girl of about nine or ten, working as a scullery maid in a great Munchkinland house under a name that is not hers. She has been passed from hand to hand since infancy and told almost nothing about where she came from. Watchful, largely silent, and far more interested in water and weather than in people, she is the descendant of the Wicked Witch of the West, and the adults who know it have agreed that she is safer not knowing.
characters.name: Rain

characters.description: Lady Glinda, once the most celebrated woman in Oz and briefly its Throne Minister, now a widow of enormous wealth and dwindling influence, keeping to her late husband's Munchkinland estate while the country falls apart around her. Vain, and shrewder than she allows anyone to see, she is hosting an occupying army in her own house under the polite fiction that they are guests.
characters.name: Glinda

characters.description: The courteous, capable officer of Loyal Oz who billets his men on Lady Glinda's estate and behaves throughout as a guest rather than an occupier. He has commanded in this manner before, and his manners have never once prevented him from carrying out an order.
characters.name: General Cherrystone

characters.description: Lady Glinda's lady's maid, elderly, rigidly proper, and made frantic by the presence of soldiers in the house. Her devotion to her mistress's dignity outlasts every practical reason for it.
characters.name: Miss Murth

characters.description: The Cowardly Lion, no longer in anybody's employ since he defaulted on the Emperor's commission, travelling with the Clock of the Time Dragon company. Protective, anxious and habitually pessimistic, he has spent the years since guarding the Witch's book of magic and the people connected to it.
characters.name: Brrr

characters.description: The foul-tempered dwarf who owns the Clock of the Time Dragon, a travelling prophetic theatre he insists is older than Oz and that he serves rather than commands. He decides where the company goes by consulting the Clock, and he is rarely willing to explain himself to anyone.
characters.name: Mr. Boss

characters.description: A Munchkinlander formerly of the Cloister of Saint Glinda, who walked out of the convent to travel with the Clock company and married its dwarf. She keeps the party fed and dosed out of a considerable knowledge of what grows beside the road.
characters.name: Little Daffy

characters.description: A veiled, withdrawn woman travelling with the Clock company, born Nor in the Vinkus household of Kiamo Ko and carried off from it as a child by Emerald City soldiers. What was done to her in the years that followed left her unable to be touched, and she has built a life out of keeping her distance from everyone, including those who love her.
characters.name: Ilianora

characters.description: The Witch's presumed son, now a grown man living hidden in the countryside and wanting nothing to do with Oz's politics. He has spent ten years keeping his daughter's existence secret, which has meant not raising her, and he has no idea how to be her father now that she has been brought to him.
characters.name: Liir

characters.description: A Quadling woman with a gift for sensing the present moment, Liir's partner and Rain's mother, who plays a stringed instrument called a domingon. She gave her daughter away in infancy to keep her alive, a decision she has never explained to the girl's satisfaction.
characters.name: Candle

characters.description: The Eminence of Munchkinland, the sorceress who governs the seceded province and prosecutes its war against Loyal Oz. A shape-shifter of formidable skill and equally formidable vanity, she is a great deal older and better established than her sudden public prominence suggests.
characters.name: La Mombey

characters.description: A quick, restless boy at the boarding school where Rain is hidden, raised by a guardian he speaks of with unease and glad of any distance he can get from her. He is the first person Rain chooses for herself, and the two of them become inseparable.
characters.name: Tip

characters.description: A kitchen servant at the boarding school, roughly Rain's age, with no illusions about her position and no intention of complaining about it. She is one of the few people who treats the strange new girl as entirely ordinary.
characters.name: Scarly

characters.description: The ruler of Loyal Oz and the dead Witch's younger brother, who governs as a living saint and has made a state religion of himself. He has spent years hunting the Grimmerie and the last of his own family, with no evident curiosity about which of them he is related to.
characters.name: Shell Thropp

recaps.ending: The war ends less in victory than in exhaustion and a change of legitimacy. La Mombey's great secret is exposed: Tip, the boy Rain loves, has been Ozma Tippetarius all along, the rightful heir to the throne of Oz, taken as an infant and held under a shape-changing spell so that Munchkinland's ruler could govern in her place. The spell is broken. Ozma is restored to her own form and inherits a divided country she never asked for, and Rain loses her first love in the process, because the person who comes out of the spell is not the boy who went into it. Dorothy is spared the sentence Munchkinland passed on her and is finally returned to her own world, closing the account that opened when a house fell on Nessarose. The Clock of the Time Dragon company, having spent three books guarding the Witch's inheritance, is released from the duty. Rain concludes that there is nowhere in Oz the Grimmerie can safely rest, not the Emperor's church, not Munchkinland's sorceress, not her own family, and that she is the only person left with no reason to want to use it. She takes the book and Elphaba's broom and flies west, out over the desert and the sea, past the edge of everything Oz has mapped, leaving her parents, her friends and Ozma behind her. The series closes with the Witch's granddaughter carrying the Witch's magic out of Oz altogether.
recaps.in_short: A third accident throws Dorothy back into Oz, into a country at war with itself: Munchkinland has seceded under the sorceress La Mombey, and Loyal Oz, ruled by the Emperor Apostle, is fighting it for Restwater and the water supply of the whole land. Rain, a green-skinned girl descended from the Wicked Witch of the West, is a scullery maid on Lady Glinda's estate, told nothing of who she is. When Glinda freezes the lake to stall the invasion and is arrested for treason, Rain is carried off with the Witch's book of magic by the Clock of the Time Dragon company, restored to the parents who gave her up, and then hidden at a boarding school, where she falls in love with a boy called Tip. Dorothy, meanwhile, is tried in Munchkinland for the deaths of both Witches and sentenced to die. In the end Tip is revealed to be Ozma, the rightful heir to Oz, hidden all her life by La Mombey under a spell. Her restoration takes the ground out from under the war, Dorothy is sent home, and Rain, deciding that no one in Oz should hold the Grimmerie, carries it out of the country on the Witch's broom and over the sea.

recaps.text: Previously in the series: Elphaba Thropp, born green, became the Wizard's most determined enemy and then the figure Oz remembers as the Wicked Witch of the West. She died at Kiamo Ko when Dorothy, a girl from another world, threw water on her, leaving behind a book of magic called the Grimmerie, a broom, and Liir, a boy she never acknowledged as her son. In Son of a Witch, Liir hunted for Nor, the girl carried off from Kiamo Ko by soldiers, served in the Emperor's forces, and destroyed the secret dragon stables that had been terrorizing Oz. Nursed back from the fall that followed by a Quadling girl called Candle, he learned that the throne had passed to an Emperor Apostle who rules Oz as a living saint and who is Elphaba's own brother, Shell. Candle bore Liir a green-skinned daughter and hid her from the Emperor's men. In A Lion Among Men, Brrr, the Cowardly Lion, was sent by that court to interrogate Yackle, an ancient woman who could not die, and came away instead with the Grimmerie, which he carried into the keeping of the travelling Clock of the Time Dragon company. Oz has meanwhile split in two: Munchkinland has seceded under the sorceress La Mombey, and Loyal Oz is fighting it for Restwater, the lake the country's water comes from.

A third journey brings Dorothy back to Oz, thrown there by an earthquake in her own country. In Munchkinland, Lady Glinda has retired to her late husband's estate at Mockbeggar Hall, where a Loyal Oz force under General Cherrystone has installed itself on the pretence of protecting her. Among her servants is a green-skinned girl called Rain, kept ignorant of her own name and family for her safety, and among her possessions is the Grimmerie, left in her keeping. Glinda works out what Cherrystone is actually doing: building a fleet in secret, inside her own outbuildings, in order to seize Restwater and with it the water supply of the entire country. Having no army, she uses the book, and freezes the lake. It buys Munchkinland time and costs her everything she has left. She is arrested for treason and confined in her own house, and Rain is got out of Mockbeggar with the Grimmerie, into the hands of the travelling company that has been shadowing her.

Rain travels with the Clock of the Time Dragon: the dwarf Mr. Boss, his wife Little Daffy, the veiled Ilianora, and Brrr the Cowardly Lion, all of whom know exactly who she is and none of whom will tell her much of it. The Clock stages its prophetic tableaux for village audiences and steers the company by a logic of its own. Rain carries the Grimmerie without being able to read it and without wanting it. She is a difficult child to protect: incurious about her own history, attached to nothing and nobody, and drawn far more strongly to water than to any of the adults arranging her life. The war closes the roads around them, the Emperor's ministry is hunting both the book and the Witch's line, and the company concludes that the girl cannot stay on the road.

Rain is brought to a hidden house near Restwater and handed over to her parents. Liir and Candle gave her away as an infant to keep the Emperor's men from finding a green-skinned child, and neither of them has any idea how to undo ten years of that decision now. Rain, for her part, does not particularly want parents. The three of them keep house together uneasily while the armies manoeuvre for the lake, and Rain spends her time in the water, where she is more at home than anyone around her can account for. The Grimmerie, which nobody under that roof will use, sits there as a standing invitation to whoever finds them.

Dorothy, at large in Oz again, is taken into custody in Munchkinland and put on trial for the deaths of the two Witches: Nessarose, killed when Dorothy's house fell on her, and Elphaba, killed by a bucket of water. The proceedings are a political performance staged by La Mombey, the Eminence of Munchkinland, for a country that needs an enemy, and Dorothy's defence, that she intended none of it, is beside the point. Brrr is dragged into the case on her account and finds his own history put on public display alongside hers. Dorothy is convicted and sentenced to death. Meanwhile the war for Restwater grinds forward, and it becomes clear that Rain's family cannot stay hidden much longer.

With the house by the lake no longer safe, Rain is put out of reach again: enrolled under a false name at St. Prowd's, a boarding school, where a green-skinned girl is explained away and expected to keep her head down. She is bad at being a schoolgirl and good at being ignored, until two people make the place bearable. Scarly, a kitchen servant, treats her as entirely ordinary. Tip, a restless boy uneasy about the guardian who raised him, becomes the first person Rain has ever chosen for herself, and the two of them fall in love with the completeness available only at that age. For a while Rain has something like an ordinary life. It does not hold: the war reaches the city, the school empties, and the people hunting the Witch's line are closing on her.

Rain's parentage stops being a secret. The Emperor Apostle, Shell Thropp, who rules Loyal Oz as a living saint, is her great-uncle, and he and La Mombey now want the same two things: the Grimmerie, and the last of Elphaba's line. Rain is moved through a country at war, in and out of the Emerald City, hidden and found and hidden again, while the adults who have spent her whole life managing her are scattered by the fighting. She begins, for the first time, to use the book rather than merely carry it, and to treat being the Witch's granddaughter as a fact about herself rather than only a danger. Tip goes with her.

The war reaches its crisis, and with it the question of who has any right to govern Oz at all. La Mombey's hold on Munchkinland rests on a deception decades old: the boy Tip is not a boy and never was a commoner. He is Ozma, the rightful heir to the throne of Oz, taken as an infant and kept all his life under a shape-changing spell. The spell is broken, and Tip becomes the young woman Ozma Tippetarius, to the dismay of both of them. Rain loses the person she loved on the terms she loved him, and Ozma is handed a country she never asked for. Rain uses the Grimmerie herself, at real cost, and Dorothy's sentence is not carried out. With a legitimate heir restored, the war between Loyal Oz and Munchkinland loses the ground it had been standing on.

Oz settles into an aftermath rather than a victory. Ozma is restored and left to make what she can of a divided country. Dorothy, who has been the pretext for a great deal of the trouble, is finally sent back to her own world for good. Rain is left holding the one object nobody in Oz should have, and she decides that the Grimmerie has no safe keeper anywhere in the country: not the Emperor's church, not Munchkinland's sorceress, not her own parents. So she takes it out of Oz herself, flying west on the Witch's broom, over the desert and out across the sea beyond the edge of every map Oz possesses. She goes alone, leaving her parents, the Clock company and the girl who used to be Tip behind her. The book closes with Rain out past Oz altogether, in the water she has been drawn to since she was a child, and with the Witch's inheritance out of Ozian hands at last.

characters.description: A capable, strong-willed Englishwoman who served as a combat nurse during the Second World War and is now on a second honeymoon in the Scottish Highlands in 1945, reconnecting with her historian husband. Practical, blunt, and skilled in medicine, she is used to hardship and unafraid to speak her mind. Her nursing knowledge and level head become vital when she is suddenly cut off from everything familiar.
characters.name: Claire Randall

characters.description: Claire's husband, a gentle Oxford-trained historian recently returned from wartime service. In Inverness he pursues his passion for genealogy, researching his own ancestors in the region. Scholarly and mild-mannered, he is devoted to Claire as the couple try to rebuild their marriage after years apart during the war.
characters.name: Frank Randall

characters.description: A captain of English dragoons in the Scottish Highlands of 1743, and, unsettlingly, a near-perfect likeness of Claire's own husband, whose distant ancestor he is. Cold, cruel, and dangerous, he wields the authority of the occupying English army with sadistic pleasure. From their first meeting he is a menacing figure, and he becomes a persistent threat to Claire and those she comes to care for.
characters.name: Jonathan Randall

characters.description: A dour, weathered Highlander of few words who rides with the clansmen who take Claire in. Gruff on the surface but steadfast and shrewd, he is a loyal kinsman and protector to the younger warrior in the party, and he keeps a watchful, skeptical eye on the strange Englishwoman thrust among them.
characters.name: Murtagh Fraser

characters.description: The war chief of Clan MacKenzie and brother to its laird, a forceful, charismatic, and ambitious man who leads the party that first takes Claire. Bold and politically cunning, he manages the clan's fighting men and its money, and he is deeply invested in Scottish causes. He treats Claire with suspicion, unsure whether she is a spy.
characters.name: Dougal MacKenzie

characters.description: The laird of Clan MacKenzie, who rules from Castle Leoch despite a crippling illness that has twisted his legs and pains him constantly. Sharp, patient, and calculating, he governs through intelligence and diplomacy rather than physical strength, and he weighs carefully what to make of the unexpected Englishwoman brought into his hall.
characters.name: Colum MacKenzie

characters.description: A young Highland warrior of Clan MacKenzie, injured when Claire first tends him. Tall, red-haired, and good-humored, he is brave, honorable, and better educated than his rough life suggests, carrying the scars and the price of an outlaw's past under English persecution. Kind and quick-witted, he becomes Claire's closest companion in a world where she has no one else to trust.
characters.name: Jamie Fraser

characters.description: The warm, bustling, and formidable housekeeper who runs the domestic life of Castle Leoch. Kind-hearted and endlessly capable, she takes Claire under her wing on arrival, providing food, clothing, and a measure of welcome amid the wary strangers of the clan.
characters.name: Mrs. Fitzgibbons

characters.description: A striking, sharp-tongued local woman married to the district's procurator fiscal, known for her deep knowledge of plants and folk remedies. She befriends Claire, sharing an interest in herbs and healing, though there is something knowing and slightly unsettling about her, and whispers of the uncanny cling to her reputation.
characters.name: Geillis Duncan

characters.description: Jamie's fierce, clever elder sister, who has managed the family's Highland estate through hard and dangerous years. Proud, sharp, and devoted to her home and kin, she has weathered great trials with courage and is not easily cowed by anyone, including her long-absent brother when he returns.
characters.name: Jenny Murray

recaps.ending: Claire has chosen the past and Jamie over her old life, but their peace is shattered when Jamie is arrested and imprisoned at Wentworth Prison, condemned to hang. There the sadistic Captain Jonathan Randall subjects him to horrifying torture and sexual assault, breaking his body and nearly his spirit. Claire, refusing to abandon him, organizes a daring rescue with the help of Jamie's kinsmen and frees him. They flee across the sea to the sanctuary of a French abbey, where Claire fights to heal not only Jamie's ruined body but the deep psychological wounds Randall inflicted, ultimately forcing a painful, cathartic confrontation with his trauma so he can begin to recover. As the novel closes, Jamie is slowly mending and the couple, bound more tightly than ever by what they have survived, learn that Claire is carrying his child. They look ahead to an uncertain future in a France where Jacobite plotting is stirring, their story left poised on the edge of new dangers to come.

Stranded and unable to return home, Claire uses her medical skill to survive and grows close to a brave young Highlander, Jamie Fraser. To protect her from English jurisdiction, she is compelled to marry Jamie, and their marriage of convenience becomes a deep and passionate love. Caught between two eras and two men, and hunted by the sadistic Captain Randall, Claire chooses to stay in the past with Jamie. recaps.text: In 1945, Claire Randall, a former army nurse, is holidaying in the Scottish Highlands with her husband Frank, a historian tracing his ancestors. Visiting an ancient ring of standing stones, Claire touches one and is suddenly transported back to the year 1743. Disoriented in a wild and dangerous era, she is accosted by a British army officer, Captain Jonathan Randall, who is the startling image of her own husband and his distant forebear. She is then seized by a band of Highland clansmen of the MacKenzies, among them a wounded young man she tends with her nursing skills, and carried off to their stronghold, Castle Leoch, where she is regarded with deep suspicion as a possible English spy and finds herself unable to explain who or what she really is.

At Castle Leoch, Claire is taken in and set to work as a healer, her medical knowledge earning her a place while her strange manner keeps the clan wary. She meets the shrewd, ailing laird Colum MacKenzie and his forceful war-chief brother Dougal, who cannot decide whether she is friend, spy, or something stranger, and she grows closer to the good-natured young warrior, Jamie Fraser, learning the burdens of his outlawed past. Kept as a guarded guest, Claire secretly plots how she might return to the standing stones and her own time, all the while adjusting to the harsh, precarious life of the eighteenth-century Highlands and the clan politics swirling around her.

Claire travels with Dougal and a party of clansmen as they ride the countryside collecting the laird's rents, and she glimpses the undercurrents of Scottish resistance to English rule. The threat posed by Captain Randall, who has legal power over Claire as an Englishwoman, grows more acute. To place her beyond his reach under the law, Dougal contrives that she marry a Scot, and she is wed to Jamie Fraser in a hasty arrangement meant purely for her protection. What begins as a marriage of necessity quickly deepens, and Claire finds herself drawn to Jamie far more than she expected, even as her heart remains torn between the husband she left behind and the life taking shape around her.

Claire and Jamie's marriage grows into a genuine and passionate bond, though Claire never abandons the hope of returning to her own time. Seizing a chance, she slips away toward the standing stones, only to be captured by Captain Randall and brought to Fort William, where his cruelty is on full display. Jamie stages a bold and reckless rescue, breaking in to save her and defying the English officer directly. The escape deepens the danger surrounding them and the enmity between Jamie and Randall, and it forces Claire to weigh, more seriously than ever, where and with whom she truly belongs as the couple flee back toward safety.

Suspicion of witchcraft falls on Claire, and she is seized along with the herb-wise Geillis Duncan and put on trial, in mortal danger until Jamie arrives to save her. In the aftermath Geillis reveals a secret that shakes Claire: she too came from another century through the stones, a committed Jacobite who came to influence history. At the standing stones Claire finally tells Jamie the truth about where and when she is from, and he gives her the choice to return to her old life; she chooses to stay with him. Jamie then brings Claire home to his family estate, Lallybroch, where he reclaims his place as laird and she meets his fierce sister Jenny. For a time they build a life there, but the shadow of the English and of Randall continues to loom over them.

Their fragile peace is torn apart when Jamie is captured and imprisoned at Wentworth Prison under sentence of death, where Captain Randall subjects him to brutal torture and sexual assault that nearly destroys him body and soul. Claire refuses to give him up for lost and, with the help of Jamie's kin, carries out a desperate rescue that frees him. The couple escapes across the sea to a French abbey, where Claire labors to heal Jamie's shattered body and mind, at last driving him through a harrowing confrontation with his trauma so that he can begin to recover. As the story ends, Jamie is slowly mending, the two are more deeply bound than ever by all they have endured, and Claire discovers that she is pregnant, carrying their child into an uncertain future amid the gathering intrigues of Jacobite France.
